components.name: AlertDialog

usage.description:
AlertDialog asks the user to confirm a destructive or irreversible action before it happens. Use it for things like deleting content, revoking access, or discarding unsaved changes.

It implements the WAI-ARIA APG [Alert Dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/): `role="alertdialog"`, a title linked by `aria-labelledby`, a consequence description linked by `aria-describedby`, focus moved into the dialog on open and returned to the trigger on close, and no dismissal by clicking outside. Escape cancels.

AlertDialog passes its requested width through to Dialog, which clamps the surface to the container and dynamic viewport with token gutters. Generic Dialog footers should wrap, but Dialog does not own action semantics or order; consumer composition controls that. AlertDialog owns its confirmation semantics: above 640px, actions render horizontally and may move onto another row; at 640px and below, the destructive action appears above Cancel and both buttons fill the footer width. Button labels retain their standard single-line behavior. The breakpoint follows available width, not pointer or hover capability. The body scrolls when block space is constrained.

For cases where you want to show an alert without managing open state, use the `useImperativeAlertDialog` hook: call `alert.show(options)` and render `alert.element` in your tree.

bestPractices.description: Make the action button label specific: "Delete project" is better than "OK" or "Confirm".
Describe what will happen in the description so the user knows the consequences before confirming.
Keep the cancel button as the least-destructive focus target. On narrow screens the destructive action is visually and structurally above Cancel, but Cancel still receives initial focus.
Use concise, specific action labels. Above 640px, complete buttons may move onto another row; at 640px and below, the destructive action appears above Cancel and both buttons fill the footer width.
Use AlertDialog for non-destructive actions; use a standard Dialog instead.
Rely on color alone to signal danger; the action label itself should say what will happen.
Close the dialog from onAction before the work finishes; hold it open with isActionLoading and call onOpenChange(false) when the action settles.

usage.description: AppShell is the page shell for an application. It provides slots for top navigation, side navigation, banners, and main content. Use it as the root wrapper for every page. It handles responsive mobile navigation and skip-to-content automatically. Configure side nav collapse on SideNav with its collapsible prop.

bestPractices.description: Choose the right height: use "fill" for dashboards with internal scrolling and "auto" for pages that grow with content.
Set `contentPadding` based on content type: 4 for forms and settings, 0 for tables and dashboards.
Give every nav slot an accessible name. AppShell renders TopNav and SideNav as separate navigation landmarks, and a screen reader lists them by name, so pass `label` to each one.
Start the page heading inside `children`. AppShell owns the skip link, the banner landmark and the main landmark, but it renders no heading, so the first heading in the content area is the page h1.

On phones, opt the page into the full screen with `viewport-fit=cover` in the viewport meta tag (`width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover`). AppShell then extends its header under the status bar and out to the screen sides, and keeps the header's items and the end of the content inside the device's safe area. An installed web app can also draw under the status bar with `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="black-translucent">`. In landscape only the header is inset: an inline SideNav and the content's sides still reach under a notch, so keep content padding there. A shell with no header region or phone top bar keeps no top inset; keep top padding there.
Nest one AppShell inside another; it's the outermost layout frame.
Use for sub-page layouts; use Layout for content areas within AppShell.
Add your own skip link or <main> element. AppShell already renders both, and a second main landmark makes the first ambiguous.

anatomy.name: Page shell
anatomy.description: Outermost application frame that owns page-level navigation, responsive shell behavior, and the main content landmark.

anatomy.name: Skip link
anatomy.description: First focusable element on the page. Visually hidden until focused, then moves focus to the main content area.

anatomy.name: Banner
anatomy.description: The banner slot, for system-wide announcements. Renders above the top nav, inside the banner landmark.

anatomy.name: Top navigation
anatomy.description: The topNav slot, typically TopNav. Below the mobile breakpoint it becomes a compact bar carrying the nav toggle.

anatomy.name: Side navigation
anatomy.description: The sideNav slot, typically SideNav. Inline above the breakpoint, moved into the mobile drawer below it.

anatomy.name: Main content
anatomy.description: children, rendered in the main landmark. Scrolls internally when height is fill, and with the page when it is auto. While it scrolls content that overflows, it is a stop in the tab order; Tab entry moves on when its first focusable element is a plain link or button, and otherwise main is one stop before it.

anatomy.name: Mobile nav drawer
anatomy.description: Generated below the breakpoint from the nav slots unless mobileNav disables or replaces it. A modal dialog: it traps focus and returns focus to the toggle on close.

props.name: children
props.description: Main content area, rendered inside a <main> element.

props.name: contentPadding
props.description: Padding for the main content area. Set based on the dominant content pattern: 4 (16px) for forms/settings/text, 0 for dashboards/maps/tables. Override individual sections with Section.

props.name: topNav
props.description: Top navigation slot, typically TopNav.

props.name: sideNav
props.description: Side navigation slot, typically SideNav.

props.name: mobileNav
props.description: Mobile navigation configuration. Accepts false (disable), a config object (tune auto behavior), or ReactNode (full custom drawer). The config object is {hasToggle?: boolean, isOpen?: boolean, onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void, content?: ReactNode, breakpoint?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | 'none', defaultIsMobile?: boolean}; breakpoint defaults to 'md', resolves through the nearest Theme's widthBreakpoints, and switches to the wider layout at equality. 'none' is always non-mobile and ignores defaultIsMobile.

props.name: banner
props.description: Banner slot for system-wide announcements, placed above the topNav.

props.name: height
props.description: Height behavior: 'fill' makes the shell fill the viewport (100dvh) with independent scroll containers; 'auto' lets the shell grow with content and uses sticky positioning for nav.

props.name: variant
props.description: Navigation background style controlling how nav areas contrast with content. 'wash' uses wash background, 'surface' uses surface background, 'section' adds dividers between nav and content, 'elevated' uses wash nav with elevated surface content and border radius.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

usage.description: Maintains a fixed width-to-height ratio for its children as its container resizes. Use it for media containers like videos, images, thumbnails, or any content that needs consistent proportions. It takes its width from the container and derives its height from the ratio, so it needs an ancestor with a definite width.

bestPractices.description: Express the ratio as a fraction for readability — `ratio={16 / 9}` rather than `ratio={1.78}`. It is a number, so the string form `ratio="16/9"` is a type error.
Use for media that needs consistent proportions across screen sizes.
Use `fit="cover"` for images and video so the component sizes the child; the child should not repeat `width`/`height`/`objectFit` styles.
Pass one child. With `fit` set, every direct child is stretched to fill the box, so put an overlay or caption inside a single wrapper child rather than passing it as a second child.
Describe media children with `alt`, or `alt=""` when the image is decorative. AspectRatio adds no role and no accessible name of its own, so the child carries the whole accessible description.

For a breakpoint-dependent ratio, override the ratio responsively: pass an `aspectRatio` rule via `xstyle` (StyleX), or override `aspect-ratio` from your own unlayered CSS under a `@media`/`@container` rule; component styles live in the `astryx-base` cascade layer, so unlayered consumer CSS wins. Give an `xstyle` rule a `default` branch alongside the conditional one (`{default: 3, '@container ...': '3 / 2'}`); with only the conditional branch the ratio is unset outside the query and the box collapses.
Use for general layout containers; use standard layout components instead.
Nest AspectRatio containers; one level is sufficient.
Constrain the height on its own. The width comes from the container, so a `height` or `maxHeight` by itself clamps the box off ratio; pair it with `width: "auto"` to size from the height instead.
Place it in a shrink-to-fit parent such as `inline-flex`, `width: fit-content` or a floated box. It contributes no intrinsic width there and collapses to zero.

anatomy.name: Ratio box
anatomy.description: The outer element that holds the aspect ratio and clips overflow. Carries the `astryx-aspect-ratio` theme target, and the elliptical clip when `shape` is `ellipse`.

anatomy.name: Content slot
anatomy.description: A wrapper that fills the ratio box and positions the child. With `fit` set it also sizes the child; without it the child styles itself.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Aspect ratio as width/height (e.g. 16/9, 1). Emitted as a class-level declaration (never inline), so `xstyle` rules or unlayered consumer CSS can override it responsively.

props.name: shape
props.description: Container shape. Both respect the `ratio`. `ellipse` clips to an oval (a circle when `ratio={1}`).

props.name: fit
props.description: How the child is sized inside the ratio box. `cover` fills and crops media, `contain` fills and letterboxes, `center` keeps the natural size centered. When omitted, the child styles itself.

props.name: children
props.description: Content positioned absolutely to fill the container.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

usage.description: Avatar represents a person or team with a profile photo, initials, or a default icon. Use it in comment headers, contact lists, chat messages, user cards, and anywhere you need to identify someone visually.

bestPractices.description: Always pass a name so the avatar can show initials if the photo fails to load, and so screen readers can announce who it represents.
Pick a size that matches the context: xsm or sm for inline mentions, md or lg for lists and cards, xl for profile headers.
Add a status dot when knowing someone's availability matters, like in chat or team views.
When wrapping an Avatar in your own Tooltip or HoverCard, set tooltip={false} so the built-in name tooltip does not overlap yours.
Give every interactive avatar (href or onClick) a name or alt. It is the control's accessible name, and it warns in development when it is missing.
Rely on a status label to name an interactive avatar. "Online" says nothing about where the link goes.
Use Avatar for logos, product images, or anything that isn't a person or team. Use an image or icon instead.
Use xstyle or className to override shape. Use the shape prop instead so themes can control it globally.

anatomy.name: Status dot

props.name: fallbackSrc

props.name: name
props.description: User name for initials and alt text.

props.name: alt

props.name: size
props.description: Avatar size: named sizes are 'xsm' (20px), 'sm' (24px), 'md' (36px), 'lg' (48px), and 'xl' (128px); numeric sizes must be one of the pixel values listed in the type. Inside an AvatarGroup, the group's size always overrides this prop, including when the group uses its default size.

props.name: shape
props.description: Shape variant of the avatar. 'circle' (default) stays fully round. 'rounded' uses the element radius token so it matches UI corner rounding and can be set globally via theme. props.name: status
props.description: Corner content for status indicators. Reporting goes through context, so it still works when the dot sits inside a wrapper component of your own.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip shown on hover and keyboard focus. Omitted or true shows the avatar's name; a string shows that text instead; false shows no tooltip. Not auto-disabled when wrapped in your own Tooltip/HoverCard. Set tooltip={false} if you supply your own overlay. No tooltip is shown when tooltip is true/omitted and there is no name.

props.name: href
props.description: When set, the avatar renders as an interactive link (`<a>` or a custom link component) pointing here. This follows the same element-swap rule as Button. Requires a meaningful accessible name via `alt` or `name`: an interactive avatar without one warns in development. Inside an AvatarGroup, interactive avatars share a single Tab stop and are reached with arrow keys.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component used when `href` is set (e.g. `next/link`). Overrides the provider-level LinkProvider default. Only applies with `href`.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target attribute. Only applies with `href`.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link rel attribute. Only applies with `href`.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. When set without `href`, the avatar renders as a focusable `<button type="button">`. Requires a meaningful accessible name via `alt` or `name`: an interactive avatar without one warns in development.

components.name: AvatarGroup

usage.description: AvatarGroup displays multiple avatars in an overlapping row with an optional overflow indicator. Uses a compositional API: pass Avatar children directly so each avatar can carry its own props (status dots, click handlers, etc.).

bestPractices.description: Slice the list yourself and pass only the avatars you want visible; 3-5 is typical. The group renders exactly the children it is given and never slices for you.
Use AvatarGroupOverflow for custom overflow content like a popover trigger or "add member" button.
Pass status dots, click handlers, or tooltips directly on each Avatar child.
Wrap an Avatar child in HoverCard or Tooltip to show more on hover; the avatars still overlap. Set tooltip={false} on the wrapped Avatar so its built-in name tooltip does not compete.

Make avatars interactive with href or onClick to link to profiles. Interactive avatars share a single Tab stop; arrow keys move between them, and the group announces a keyboard hint to assistive tech. This follows the WAI-ARIA APG roving tabindex technique for managing focus in a composite: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex
Don't nest AvatarGroups; use a single group with all avatars.
Don't set size on the child avatars. The group's size wins over each child's own size prop, including when the group leaves size at its default, so a child's size is silently ignored inside a group.

components.description: Overflow indicator for AvatarGroup. Shows a compact count for hidden avatars and can render custom count text or act as a button.

props.name: count
props.description: The number of hidden avatars. Used for the default `+N` label and the accessible label.

props.name: children

usage.description: AvatarGroupOverflow appears at the end of an AvatarGroup to summarize people who are not shown individually. Use it when a group is sliced to a small number of visible avatars but the hidden count still matters.

bestPractices.description: Pass the real hidden count to `count` so the accessible label matches the visible indicator.
Use short custom text such as `+12` or `99+`. The indicator is circular for short counts and grows into a pill for wider counts so the number always fits.
Provide `onClick` when the overflow opens a member list, popover, or detail view.
Do not pass custom text that disagrees with `count`; `count` continues to provide the accessible label.
Do not use long labels inside the indicator; place longer participant details next to the group instead.

    <Avatar key={user.id} src={user.src} name={user.name} />
  ))}
  <AvatarGroupOverflow count={users.length - 3} />
</AvatarGroup>

components.name: AvatarStatusDot
components.description: Size-aware status indicator dot that reads avatar size from context and scales proportionally. Each variant pairs a colour with a distinct built-in shape (filled, ring, minus) so status is never conveyed by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1).

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic variant pairing colour with a distinct shape: success = filled green dot, neutral = grey ring, error = red dot with a minus bar.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label describing the status. Inside an Avatar it is composed into the avatar's accessible name (e.g. "Jane Doe, Online"); the Avatar root is role="img", which prunes child semantics, so the composed name is how the status reaches assistive tech. Standalone dots expose role="img" with this label directly.

props.name: icon

usage.description: Badge highlights a status or category at a glance. Use it sparingly: only when a value represents a distinct state (Active, Failed) or a grouping tag (Engineering, Design). Most metadata (dates, durations, counts, descriptions) should be plain description text, not badges.

bestPractices.description: Every status badge steals attention. Only badge states where the user needs to notice or act: errors, warnings, items requiring follow-up. If no action is needed, plain text is fine.
Use success, warning, and error variants only for system status that demands attention: "Failed", "Degraded", "Action Required". These have bold solid backgrounds designed to stand out.
Use color variants (blue, purple, teal, etc.) for category tags that group or classify items: team names, content types, priority levels.
Keep labels to one or two words. If you need more detail, put it in surrounding text instead of the badge.
Add an icon when it helps identify the badge type quickly, but always include a text label alongside it.

Apply a "success" badge to every healthy/active/normal item. If all rows show green "Active" badges, none stand out; the badge adds noise, not information. Show only the states that need user attention (errors, warnings, pending actions).
Use badges for metadata. Durations ("6h window"), counts ("12 trigger types"), dates, and descriptions are not statuses or categories; use description text (Text with type="supporting") instead.
Use semantic status variants (success, warning, error, info) for categories or informational content. These are visually loud and should only indicate system state.

Repeat the same badge in every row of a table or list. If the same value appears in most rows, it's not adding information; use plain text for common states and reserve badges for the exceptional ones.
Make badges clickable; they are read-only indicators. Use a button or link if the user needs to take action.

usage.description: Banner shows a persistent message at the top of a page or section. Use it for form errors, system updates, maintenance notices, or success confirmations that the user needs to see until they act on it.

bestPractices.description: Pick a status that matches the message: info for updates, warning for caution, error for problems, success for confirmations.
Use the card container inside page content and the section container for full-width messages that span the entire page.
Make info and success banners dismissable. Keep error banners visible until the user fixes the issue.
Keep titles short and scannable: "Payment failed" not "There was a problem processing your most recent payment."
Use Banner for short-lived messages that disappear on their own; use Toast instead.
Stack multiple banners with the same status; combine related messages into one banner.

Set collapsible={false} when the user needs the content to act on the message, like the list of fields that failed validation. Keep the default toggle when the detail is long enough to bury the banner's own message.

Banner status controls color and icon only; it does not create a live region. Announce async outcomes from the transition handler with useAnnounce. Add an explicit role="status" only when the visible banner is intended as a persistent semantic mirror; reserve role="alert" for genuinely urgent, interruptive content.
Rely on the status color or icon alone to carry meaning; say which status it is in the title text, because the icon is decorative to a screen reader.

anatomy.name: Content surface
anatomy.description: Secondary surface for extra detail below the status surface, like a list of errors. Sits behind an expand/collapse toggle by default; set collapsible={false} to keep it visible.

components.description: Composable combobox engine providing a bare input, search, keyboard navigation, and a styled result dropdown. It renders no input wrapper, border, or selected-value token. Typeahead and Tokenizer compose it for standard fields.

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: Bare combobox input. The caller supplies its visible field chrome and accessible name.

anatomy.name: Loading status
anatomy.description: Named Spinner shown beside the input while an asynchronous source is pending, unless a composed owner takes over the busy indicator lane.

anatomy.name: Dropdown
anatomy.description: Anchored listbox surface containing current search or bootstrap results.

anatomy.name: Empty state
anatomy.description: Disabled listbox option shown after a completed search returns no results.

anatomy.name: Result group heading
anatomy.description: Visible label for a group of result options.

anatomy.name: Result row
anatomy.description: Option wrapper that owns highlight, selection, pointer, and keyboard behavior.

anatomy.name: Default item content
anatomy.description: TypeaheadItem label and optional supporting content rendered inside a result row.

anatomy.name: Caller-rendered item content

anatomy.name: Selected result state

usage.description: Composable combobox engine providing a bare input, search, keyboard navigation, and a styled result dropdown. It renders no input wrapper, border, or selected-value token. Typeahead and Tokenizer compose it for standard fields.

bestPractices.description: Use Typeahead or Tokenizer for standard fields; they wrap BaseTypeahead with input chrome and selected-value rendering it intentionally omits.
Provide your own visible label or aria-label and custom input wrapper so the bare combobox has an accessible name, focus treatment, border, and layout.
Pass anchorRef pointing to your wrapper so the dropdown positions against your custom input chrome, not just the bare input element.
Expect input chrome or selected-value rendering. BaseTypeahead is an engine; the caller owns those visible parts.
Use BaseTypeahead when Typeahead or Tokenizer would suffice; the extra wrapper and styling work is only justified for truly custom compositions.
Treat Escape as cancellation of pending source work. It hides the current popup, but a late response can reopen it.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods. `search(query, context)` may call `context.update(items)` to show matches it already has before it returns; the value it returns is the final list, and every list after the first for a query keeps the shown rows first and adds new rows after them.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected item.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the selection changes.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum dropdown items to display.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Requested dropdown width in pixels before viewport clamping.

props.name: minQueryLength
props.description: Minimum query length before the search source is queried. Below it no search runs and the menu stays closed.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when the query matched nothing. Takes a ReactNode, so the dead end can carry a link or a create row. Announced in a polite live region as the text it renders, read from the DOM; aria-hidden parts stay out of both, and content that renders no text announces nothing. null counts as not given, like undefined, and falls through to the default; pass an empty string to render nothing.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the input is disabled.

props.name: isFocusableDisabled
props.description: Keep a disabled input focusable with aria-disabled and readOnly so a caller-owned disabled reason remains discoverable. It blocks text entry, opening the results and picking a result, also from results that were open before it applied; Escape or Tab still closes them.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources, and for a source that shows local matches through `context.update` and delays its own server request.

props.name: size
props.description: Size used to scale dropdown option padding.

props.name: anchorRef
props.description: Ref to the anchor element for dropdown positioning. If not provided, the input itself is used.

props.name: inputXStyle
props.description: Additional StyleX styles for the input element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: Standard BaseProps StyleX styles applied to the input. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.

props.name: inputTabIndex
props.description: Legacy input-specific alias for native tabIndex. When provided, it takes precedence; otherwise native tabIndex is preserved.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Additional keydown handler called before internal keyboard navigation. Call e.preventDefault() to skip internal handling.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the dropdown opens or closes.

props.name: inputId
props.description: Legacy input-specific alias for native id. When provided, it takes precedence; otherwise native id is preserved.

props.name: ariaDescribedBy
props.description: Legacy input-specific alias for native aria-describedby. When provided, it takes precedence; otherwise the native attribute is preserved.

props.name: ariaLabelledBy
props.description: Legacy input-specific alias for native aria-labelledby. When provided, it takes precedence; otherwise the native attribute is preserved.

components.name: BottomSheet

children.children: Adjust the properties below, then open the preview.

components.description: A mobile touch sheet that rises from the bottom edge, with animated entrance and exit, a grab handle, optional drag-to-resize snap points, and purpose-controlled dismissal. Like Dialog, it is a padded container: content starts at the theme's bottom-sheet padding (--spacing-4 by default), and a lone Section child or bleed children such as Table and Divider align against it. A sheet always owns a native <dialog>; inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher the switcher presents and closes that dialog as the flow moves between steps. In both modes, ref and shared DOM props target the visual panel <div>. Sheets stack: a sheet opened while another is open sits on top of it, the covered sheet stays mounted and recedes, and one scrim covers the page. A sheet that closes as another opens in the same update is replaced by it, with the step-to-step handoff a multi-step flow needs.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether a standalone sheet is open. Fully controlled; pair with onOpenChange. Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: For a standalone sheet, called when it requests an open-state change. Automatic calls follow purpose: info dismisses on Escape, scrim click, or swipe; form dismisses on Escape only; required never dismisses implicitly. Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself.

props.name: finalFocusRef
props.description: Optional explicit focus-return target for a standalone sheet. Use when the opener can remount or the active element is not a reliable trigger, such as an adaptive presentation switch. Always focused when the sheet closes on its own or last; when a modal sheet is still open beneath, focus returns into that sheet (to this element if it is inside it, else the revealed panel). Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself.

props.name: purpose
props.description: Controls implicit dismissal behavior, matching Dialog. info allows Escape, scrim click, and swipe-to-dismiss. form protects entered data by blocking scrim click and swipe while allowing Escape. required blocks every implicit dismissal path and uses role='alertdialog'. Explicit controls may still update the controlled state. Works for standalone and BottomSheetSwitcher-managed sheets.

props.name: sheetId
props.description: Deprecated with BottomSheetSwitcher: give each step its own standalone sheet with isOpen instead. Still works as released: the unique ID of this sheet inside a BottomSheetSwitcher, which opens it when activeSheet matches; omit isOpen and onOpenChange when sheetId is used.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the sheet. Required; the sheet has no built-in heading to derive a name from.

props.name: children
props.description: Sheet content in a scrollable area. The named body is keyboard reachable while overflowing. Forward Tab entry may move directly to the first native link or button; input controls, composite widgets, and nested scroll areas retain the body stop. Shift+Tab from a delegated first child skips the body. Fitting content adds no body stop. The internal observed content box preserves block flow and percentage heights. If it includes a text-entry control that can bring up the mobile keyboard, use height='tall' and keep the sheet fully expanded while editing.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding of the sheet content using the spacing scale, matching Dialog. When omitted, uses the theme default for bottom sheets (--spacing-4 unless the theme sets padding on bottom-sheet). A lone Section child escapes the padding, and bleed children such as Table and Divider compensate against it. Use 0 for edge-to-edge content that supplies its own inset.

props.name: height
props.description: How tall the sheet is. Named budgets: 'hug' fits its content up to 92% of the viewport, 'capped' is a scrolling mid-height panel (~62%), and 'tall' is a pinned near-full panel (~92%) for content that streams in. Or pass a number (px) / CSS length for a custom budget. Give snapPoints to let the user drag between heights. On shorter viewports the sheet fills the available height. Only a fully expanded 'tall' sheet provides mobile-keyboard accommodation: it stays put and scrolls each focused control above the keyboard. Hug, Capped, numeric and CSS-length heights never do, and a Tall sheet stops doing it the moment the user drags it to a shorter detent, resuming when they drag it back. Outside that state the sheet neither moves nor adds keyboard scroll space, and the browser's own focus reveal is left in place; on iOS that reveal can shift the whole page.

props.name: snapPoints
props.description: Extra heights the sheet can rest at when dragged; its own height is always the tallest stop, and omitting this gives a sheet that only opens and closes. Each stop is the sheet's visible height: a number is a viewport fraction (0.5 is half the screen), '50%' the same in CSS, '320px' an absolute length. A stop of a quarter of the sheet or less is a peek: it slides away instead of reflowing, and thins the scrim.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: For a standalone BottomSheet, whether to render a scrim, the semi-transparent overlay that covers and blocks the background. true (default) uses showModal(): top layer, native focus containment, ::backdrop scrim, body scroll lock, and tap-scrim-to-dismiss when purpose='info', with the background inert. A scrim sheet also takes part in stacking (see Stacking below). false presents the sheet in the top layer as a manual popover (below the Popover API support floor, show() in page stacking order as a reduced fallback) with no scrim, no focus trap and no scroll lock, leaving the page behind interactive and scrollable; a no-scrim sheet neither stacks nor is stacked on, but no-scrim steps replace each other with the same handoff. A no-scrim sheet shown while a modal (a scrim sheet or a Dialog) that does not contain it is open is inert under that modal and stays beneath it (show(), no page-level z-index) until that modal has gone, then enters the top layer; a modal mid-exit counts as gone, and rendered inside the modal the sheet enters the top layer at once. In a multi-step flow, set hasScrim the same on every step.

anatomy.name: Sheet panel
anatomy.description: Painted surface that rises from the bottom edge and contains the sheet.

anatomy.name: Content area
anatomy.description: Padded, scrollable container that presents the caller-provided sheet content.

anatomy.name: Handle
anatomy.description: Decorative grab affordance and drag region at the top of the panel.

anatomy.name: Scrim
anatomy.description: Backdrop that dims and blocks the page in a scrim-backed presentation.

usage.description:
A mobile touch surface for filters, actions, forms, and detail views that should rise from the bottom of the viewport. For a multi-step flow, give each step its own sheet and one state value that names the open step (see Replacing a sheet); open a second sheet over the first when a step should stay visible beneath it.

Stacking. Every sheet keeps its own isOpen. Open a sheet while another scrim sheet is open and it stacks on top: the sheet beneath stays mounted with its scroll position and inputs, recedes behind the new one (the nearest covered sheet shrinks to 0.96 and lifts 8px, deeper ones to 0.92 and 16px), and is blocked from pointer, keyboard, and assistive technology by the top sheet's modal dialog. The sheets can be siblings, live in separate components, sit inside another sheet's content, or sit inside a BottomSheetSwitcher step; a whole switcher is one level, and switching its step in place does not change its position. Nothing moves in the DOM: each sheet's dialog stays where it is written, and no wrapper component is needed.

Order is open order. The top sheet is the one presented most recently that is still open; a sheet that closes and reopens comes back on top. When several sheets open in one update (a deep link into a flow), there is no open order between them, so tree order decides: a sheet below the sheets rendered in its content, siblings in the order they are written. That order is right in the first painted frame.

One scrim. Only the bottom sheet's backdrop dims the page; the backdrops of the sheets above it are transparent, so a stack never darkens per level. The dim holds steady while sheets push and pop, and if the bottom sheet closes while sheets remain above it, the next sheet's backdrop takes over in the same frame.

Dismissal. Escape, a tap on the scrim, a downward swipe, and a platform close request (Android back, a close watcher) reach only the top sheet, through that sheet's own onOpenChange, and that sheet's purpose applies: required blocks all of them, form blocks the scrim and the swipe. Nothing closes a whole stack at once; set every sheet closed in one update when a flow is done and they leave together.

Closing a covered sheet from code. Sheets rendered inside the closing sheet's content are part of it: they are presented only while it is open and leave with it. Their isOpen stays yours, as with a Dialog rendered in a closed Dialog: nothing is written to it, and a nested sheet that is still open when its host reopens is presented again, on top. Set it closed yourself when the flow is done. Sheets above the closing sheet that are not in its content stay open and keep their order; the closing sheet slides out from beneath them, and if it owned the scrim, the sheet above takes it over.

Replacing a sheet. Close the top sheet and open another in the same update (one state value that names the open step does this) and the new sheet replaces it instead of stacking on it: the new sheet rises above the one it replaces; if the replaced sheet is taller it moves down to meet the new sheet's top edge at the same time; the replaced sheet fades only after both motions finish, and is inert and hidden from assistive technology from the start. The scrim holds steady throughout, with no dip; focus moves into the new sheet; and when the flow closes, focus returns to the element that opened its first sheet, whichever sheet closed last. This is the handoff the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher ran between its steps; a multi-step flow needs no switcher: give each step its own BottomSheet and one state value. A replace happens only when exactly one sheet closes and one opens in the update, the closing sheet was the top sheet of its stack, and the move was made from inside it (the control last pressed, or with no recent press the focused element, was in the closing sheet, as a step's own Continue or Back button is); a covered sheet closing while a sheet opens, a close and an open in different updates, or a close and an open driven from a control outside the closing sheet (two unrelated owners acting at once) keep the ordinary push and pop motion and their own focus return. A replace over an open stack runs one level up and leaves the sheets beneath covered. Non-modal sheets (hasScrim={false}) replace each other the same way, with no scrim: they are hosted in the browser top layer as manual popovers, so the entering step orders above the retained one with no page-level z-index, and toasts raised before or while the sheet is open stay above it. Below the Popover API support floor (Tier 2 in the browser support guide) the sheet falls back to show() in page stacking order: usable, but with no promise over later page content. A non-modal sheet returns focus to its opener on close only while focus is still inside it; focus taken elsewhere on the live page stays there.

Focus. Opening a sheet moves focus into it, wherever the engine's native dialog focusing steps land: the panel in Chromium, the first focusable control in Firefox (a data-autofocus field only when it comes first). A step entering as a replacement focuses a data-autofocus descendant first, so a flow that opens on a field keeps the keyboard on it. Closing the top sheet returns focus into the sheet it reveals: to the control that opened it when that control is still there, otherwise to the revealed sheet's panel. When the last sheet closes, the standalone rules apply: finalFocusRef, else the element that opened the sheet, with a focus ring only after keyboard input. When every sheet of a stack closes in one update, focus returns once, to the bottom sheet's finalFocusRef or opener, after the last dialog has closed.

Caveats. A Dialog, AlertDialog, or Popover opened from a sheet paints above the sheet and does not make it recede; a sheet opened from inside that Dialog paints above the Dialog and stacks over the sheet beneath. Sheets with hasScrim={false} stay out of the stack entirely (they replace each other, but never stack, recede, or take the scrim). A sheet React hides (a suspended Suspense boundary, Activity mode="hidden") leaves the stack and closes its dialog; when it is shown again it is presented again, on top. Only sheets rendered in the same document stack; a sheet inside an iframe is its own stack.

bestPractices.description: Use for mobile-first surfaces (filters, share sheets, quick actions) where the content should rise from the bottom edge.

For a drill-in, open the next sheet over the current one and keep each sheet's isOpen where its data lives; a detail sheet can sit inside the list sheet that opens it, right next to the row. Close every sheet in one update to close the whole flow.
Pick the starting height that fits the content: 'hug' for short bounded content, 'capped' for lists, and 'tall' for forms or streaming/resizing content.
Use purpose='form' to protect entered data from scrim clicks and swipes while keeping Escape available; reserve purpose='required' for flows that must end through an explicit action.
Don't make the sheet content overly long. Break it into steps, each its own sheet, with one state value naming the open step; moving on replaces one with the next.

Don't stack more than two or three sheets: deeper sheets share the second recede step and the user has to pop them one at a time. Replace steps instead (close one, open the next in one update) when they do not need to stay visible.

props.description: Controls implicit dismissal behavior, matching Dialog. info allows Escape, scrim click, and swipe-to-dismiss. form protects entered data by blocking scrim click and swipe while allowing Escape. required blocks every implicit dismissal path and uses role='alertdialog'. Explicit controls may still update the controlled state. Works for standalone and BottomSheetSwitcher-managed sheets.

props.name: sheetId
props.description: Deprecated with BottomSheetSwitcher: give each step its own standalone sheet with isOpen instead. Still works as released: the unique ID of this sheet inside a BottomSheetSwitcher, which opens it when activeSheet matches; omit isOpen and onOpenChange when sheetId is used.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the sheet. Required; the sheet has no built-in heading to derive a name from.

props.name: children
props.description: Sheet content in a scrollable area. The named body is keyboard reachable while overflowing. Forward Tab entry may move directly to the first native link or button; input controls, composite widgets, and nested scroll areas retain the body stop. Shift+Tab from a delegated first child skips the body. Fitting content adds no body stop. The internal observed content box preserves block flow and percentage heights. If it includes a text-entry control that can bring up the mobile keyboard, use height='tall' and keep the sheet fully expanded while editing.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding of the sheet content using the spacing scale, matching Dialog. When omitted, uses the theme default for bottom sheets (--spacing-4 unless the theme sets padding on bottom-sheet). A lone Section child escapes the padding, and bleed children such as Table and Divider compensate against it. Use 0 for edge-to-edge content that supplies its own inset.

props.name: height
props.description: How tall the sheet is. Named budgets: 'hug' fits its content up to 92% of the viewport, 'capped' is a scrolling mid-height panel (~62%), and 'tall' is a pinned near-full panel (~92%) for content that streams in. Or pass a number (px) / CSS length for a custom budget. Give snapPoints to let the user drag between heights. On shorter viewports the sheet fills the available height. Only a fully expanded 'tall' sheet provides mobile-keyboard accommodation: it stays put and scrolls each focused control above the keyboard. Hug, Capped, numeric and CSS-length heights never do, and a Tall sheet stops doing it the moment the user drags it to a shorter detent, resuming when they drag it back. Outside that state the sheet neither moves nor adds keyboard scroll space, and the browser's own focus reveal is left in place; on iOS that reveal can shift the whole page.

props.name: snapPoints
props.description: Extra heights the sheet can rest at when dragged; its own height is always the tallest stop, and omitting this gives a sheet that only opens and closes. Each stop is the sheet's visible height: a number is a viewport fraction (0.5 is half the screen), '50%' the same in CSS, '320px' an absolute length. A stop of a quarter of the sheet or less is a peek: it slides away instead of reflowing, and thins the scrim.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: For a standalone BottomSheet, whether to render a scrim, the semi-transparent overlay that covers and blocks the background. true (default) uses showModal(): top layer, native focus containment, ::backdrop scrim, body scroll lock, and tap-scrim-to-dismiss when purpose='info', with the background inert. A scrim sheet also takes part in stacking (see Stacking below). false presents the sheet in the top layer as a manual popover (below the Popover API support floor, show() in page stacking order as a reduced fallback) with no scrim, no focus trap and no scroll lock, leaving the page behind interactive and scrollable; a no-scrim sheet neither stacks nor is stacked on, but no-scrim steps replace each other with the same handoff. A no-scrim sheet shown while a modal (a scrim sheet or a Dialog) that does not contain it is open is inert under that modal and stays beneath it (show(), no page-level z-index) until that modal has gone, then enters the top layer; a modal mid-exit counts as gone, and rendered inside the modal the sheet enters the top layer at once. In a multi-step flow, set hasScrim the same on every step.

anatomy.name: Sheet panel
anatomy.description: Painted surface that rises from the bottom edge and contains the sheet.

anatomy.name: Content area
anatomy.description: Padded, scrollable container that presents the caller-provided sheet content.

anatomy.name: Handle
anatomy.description: Decorative grab affordance and drag region at the top of the panel.

anatomy.name: Scrim
anatomy.description: Backdrop that dims and blocks the page in a scrim-backed presentation.

usage.description: Mobile touch surface for filters, actions, forms, and detail views that should rise from the bottom of the viewport; for a multi-step flow give each step its own sheet and one state value naming the open step: a same-update close and open is a replace handoff (entering sheet above, retained sheet aligns then fades, one steady scrim, focus back to the flow's opener on close). Open a sheet over another to stack: each sheet keeps its own isOpen, the top sheet is the most recently opened one, the covered sheet recedes and is blocked, one scrim dims the page, and dismissal pops only the top sheet. Sheets rendered in a closing sheet's content leave with it (their isOpen stays yours; they return with the host while still open); siblings above it stay open.

bestPractices.description: Use for mobile-first surfaces (filters, share sheets, quick actions) where the content should rise from the bottom edge.
Pick the starting height that fits the content: 'hug' for short bounded content, 'capped' for lists, and 'tall' for forms or streaming/resizing content.
Use purpose='form' to protect entered data from scrim clicks and swipes while keeping Escape available; reserve purpose='required' for flows that must end through an explicit action.
Don't make the sheet content overly long. Break it into steps, each its own sheet, with one state value naming the open step; moving on replaces one with the next.
Don't stack more than two or three sheets; replace steps (close one, open the next in one update) when they need not stay visible.

Long scrolling content
Multi-step flow (one sheet at a time, each step replaces the last)

Detail sheet inside the list sheet that opens it

Mobile keyboard
No scrim
Protect form input

components.description: Deprecated: write each step as its own BottomSheet with isOpen, controlled by one state value that names the open step. Closing the top sheet and opening the next in the same update, from a control inside the open step, runs the same replace handoff (see BottomSheet, Replacing a sheet), with no sheetId and no switcher; a step changed from a control outside the flow (a page control, or code after focus left the step) closes and opens with ordinary push and pop motion. BottomSheetSwitcher keeps working until a future minor release removes it: a flow used on its own behaves as released (with two fixes: a toast raised from a step renders above the flow and can be pressed, and under reduced motion its steps follow the reduced-motion rule), and a flow stacked with other sheets is one level of the stack (it recedes and is blocked when covered, shares the one scrim, and stands down from dismissal while covered). Modal and hasScrim={false} flows migrate the same way. Coordinates multiple BottomSheets as a mutually exclusive flow. One activeSheet ID selects the only interactive sheet; during a handoff, the new sheet enters above the inert previous sheet. If the new sheet is shorter, the previous sheet simultaneously moves down until their top edges align, then fades after both transforms complete. Each child sheet renders its own native <dialog>: a modal flow presents each sheet with showModal(), as a standalone modal sheet does, so the browser supplies modality (the page is inert and focus stays in the top-layer dialog, so both hold across a handoff) and the switcher holds the shared body scroll lock once for the whole modal flow. A no-scrim flow presents each sheet with show() inside the isolated flow wrapper of the switcher, which orders the step dialogs with local values; this differs from a standalone hasScrim={false} sheet, which is hosted in the top layer as a manual popover with no page-level z-index, and it is one reason to migrate. The switcher coordinates the rest: one scrim paints at a time, focus returns to the element that opened the flow, its ref, id, and data-testid resolve to the dialog hosting the active sheet, and its other dialog props and handlers apply to every sheet dialog.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref resolved to the native dialog hosting the flow: the active sheet's dialog, which changes to the next sheet's on a handoff; the exiting sheet's through its exit; and, while the flow is closed, the dialog that hosted it last (or the first mounted sheet's). It is never null while a sheet is mounted, from the first commit on. id and data-testid render on this dialog only: a flow that mounts open carries them on the active sheet's dialog in server markup too; a flow that mounts closed carries them from the first commit's synchronous re-render on, and its server markup carries them on no element. Other dialog props apply to every sheet dialog.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Called before the switcher handles a native cancel request (Escape or the platform close). Attached to every sheet dialog; the browser raises cancel on the dialog it is presenting, the active sheet's. Calling preventDefault() keeps the controlled flow open.

props.name: activeSheet
props.description: ID of the interactive BottomSheet, or null when the flow should close. Match a nested BottomSheet's unique sheetId; the previous sheet may remain visually present and inert while the new sheet enters, simultaneously align downward behind a shorter step, then fade away.

props.name: onActiveSheetChange
props.description: Called with null when the active sheet dismisses according to its purpose. Child BottomSheets may use purpose='form' or purpose='required' to limit implicit dismissal while flow controls can still use the same state setter to switch sheets or close the flow.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: Whether the sheet dialogs are modal. true presents each sheet with showModal() for a native ::backdrop, native focus containment, one body scroll lock held for the whole flow, and click-to-dismiss when the active BottomSheet has purpose='info'; only one backdrop paints at a time. false uses show() with no backdrop and leaves the page interactive; avoid transformed, contained, or clipping ancestors because a non-modal dialog remains in its containing context.

props.name: children
props.description: BottomSheets identified by unique sheetId values.

anatomy.name: Sheet dialogs
anatomy.description: One native dialog per child sheet, presented and closed by the switcher; the dialog hosting the active sheet carries the flow's ref, id, modality, and dismissal.

anatomy.name: Sheet panels
anatomy.description: Direct BottomSheet children; exactly one is interactive while a previous panel may remain visible and inert during a handoff.

anatomy.name: Scrim
anatomy.description: Native dialog backdrop shown by the default scrim-backed modal presentation; one sheet dialog paints it at a time, so a handoff never dims the page twice.

usage.description:
Deprecated: write each step as its own BottomSheet with isOpen, controlled by one state value that names the open step. Closing the top sheet and opening the next in the same update, from a control inside the open step, runs the same replace handoff (see BottomSheet, Replacing a sheet), with no sheetId and no switcher; a step changed from a control outside the flow (a page control, or code after focus left the step) closes and opens with ordinary push and pop motion. BottomSheetSwitcher keeps working until a future minor release removes it: a flow used on its own behaves as released (with two fixes: a toast raised from a step renders above the flow and can be pressed, and under reduced motion its steps follow the reduced-motion rule), and a flow stacked with other sheets is one level of the stack (it recedes and is blocked when covered, shares the one scrim, and stands down from dismissal while covered). Modal and hasScrim={false} flows migrate the same way. Set activeSheet to a nested BottomSheet's sheetId to open or switch steps, and to null to close.

Stacking. A scrim flow is one level in the stack of open sheets (see BottomSheet, Stacking). Open it while a standalone sheet is open and the flow sits on top of that sheet, which recedes and is blocked; open a standalone sheet while the flow is open, from a step's content or from anywhere else, and that sheet sits on top while the whole flow recedes as one. Switching the step in place never changes the flow's position. Escape, the scrim, a swipe, and a platform close request reach only the top level: the flow's onActiveSheetChange(null) when the flow is on top, the standalone sheet's onOpenChange(false) when that sheet is. A standalone sheet rendered inside a step's content is presented only while that step is the active one: it leaves when the flow switches step or closes, its isOpen stays yours, and it is presented again, on top, if the step returns while it is still open. Only the bottom level's backdrop dims the page. A no-scrim flow stays out of the stack.

bestPractices.description: Prefer one standalone BottomSheet per step with one state value naming the open step; the replace handoff is the same and nothing has to be nested under a switcher.

Migrate an existing flow in place: replace activeSheet / onActiveSheetChange with one step value, give each step isOpen={step === id} and a guarded onOpenChange (clear the step only if it is still the open one) in place of sheetId, remove the wrapper and move its hasScrim onto every step. Map the other switcher props: onCancel becomes a guarded onOpenChange on each step (ignore false while the flow must stay open) — a standalone sheet reports Escape, the platform close, the scrim tap and the swipe all as onOpenChange(false) with no reason, so the guard holds the step against all of them while it applies, and a veto of Escape alone has no equivalent; the only per-path lever is purpose (form keeps Escape and blocks the scrim tap and the swipe; required blocks all three and exposes the step as an alertdialog). A consumer aria-label or aria-labelledby becomes each step label, which names its dialog. ref, id, data-testid, className, style, xstyle and the other dialog props have no dialog-level equivalent: a standalone sheet sends its ref and base props to the panel div and its dialog is implementation, so a test or anchor that needs the dialog queries the panel closest("dialog"), and dialog-level styling is dropped.
Don't split information across sheets when people need to compare it; use a full-page layout that keeps the relevant content visible together instead.
Don't use a step flow when multiple panels must stay interactive or visible together; a flow intentionally selects one interactive step.

examples.label: Replacement: the same three-step flow as standalone sheets
examples.code:
const [step, setStep] = useState(null);

<>
  <Button label="Start" onClick={() => setStep('details')} />
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'details'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'details' ? null : c))} label="Details" height="hug">
    <SetupDetails />
    <Button label="Continue" onClick={() => setStep('preferences')} />
  </BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'preferences'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'preferences' ? null : c))} label="Preferences" height="hug">
    <Preferences />
    <Button label="Back" onClick={() => setStep('details')} />
    <Button label="Continue" onClick={() => setStep('confirm')} />
  </BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'confirm'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'confirm' ? null : c))} label="Confirm" height="hug">
    <Confirmation />
    <Button label="Back" onClick={() => setStep('preferences')} />
    <Button label="Done" onClick={() => setStep(null)} />
  </BottomSheet>
</>

components.name: Breadcrumbs

usage.description: Breadcrumbs show a trail of links from the root to the current page. Use them at the top of detail pages, settings panels, or anywhere the user needs to see where they are and navigate back up.

bestPractices.description: Place breadcrumbs above the page heading so the user sees their location before reading the content.
Keep labels short and match the page titles they link to: "Settings" not "Application Settings Page".
Use the supporting variant in dense UIs like admin panels or sidebars where the breadcrumb should be subtle.
Make the last item plain text, not a link; it represents the current page. The component does this automatically when you set isCurrent.

The component implements the WAI-ARIA APG Breadcrumb pattern: a labelled nav landmark wrapping an ordered list, with aria-current="page" on the current item. A crumb with a menu additionally implements the APG Menu Button pattern, opening on Enter, Space or ArrowDown and closing on Escape.
Give each trail its own label when a page renders more than one, so the nav landmarks stay distinguishable in a screen reader landmark list.
Use breadcrumbs as the primary navigation. They supplement a sidebar or top nav, not replace it.
Show breadcrumbs on top-level pages that have no parent; they add clutter without helping the user.
Let the trail grow beyond 5 levels. If you need more, consider simplifying the page hierarchy instead.
The built-in slash separator mirrors automatically in RTL. For a custom separator, leave Unicode-mirrored angle quotes such as › alone; mirror arrows and Icon separators once with rtlStyles.mirror.

Mirror a separator the bidi algorithm already mirrors. An angle-quote glyph such as › is Bidi_Mirrored, so it flips under RTL on its own and rtlStyles.mirror would flip it back. An arrow glyph such as → and any Icon separator are not, so those do need rtlStyles.mirror through xstyle.

usage.description: Button triggers an action when clicked. Use it for form submissions, confirmations, navigation, or any interaction that needs a clear call to action.

bestPractices.description: Reserve primary for the single most important action in the view. Use secondary or ghost for everything else based on emphasis.
Write labels that describe the action ("Save changes", "Delete account", "Send invite"), not vague labels like "OK" or "Click here".
Show a loading state for actions that take time, like saving or submitting, so the user knows it is working.
Always provide a label for icon-only buttons so screen readers can announce what the button does. Add a tooltip for sighted users.
For a dedicated icon-only button, use IconButton from '@astryxdesign/core/IconButton'. It is a separate component, not exported from '@astryxdesign/core/Button'.
Place more than one primary button in the same view; this dilutes the visual hierarchy.
Use the destructive variant without a confirmation step for irreversible actions like deleting data.
Use a button for navigation. If it only takes the user to another page, use a link instead. Buttons are for actions like saving, deleting, or submitting.

accessibility.name: Text label
accessibility.description: Button text must have at least 4.5:1 contrast with the button background in every state. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final background after the overlay is applied.

accessibility.name: Essential icon or spinner arc
accessibility.description: An icon used instead of text must have at least 3:1 contrast with the button background. The moving spinner arc must also meet 3:1. An icon beside a visible label does not need its own check.

accessibility.name: Badge text
accessibility.description: Badge text inside a button must have at least 4.5:1 contrast with the Badge background. Check all 14 built-in Badge colors in Rest, Hover, and Pointer down on page and surface backgrounds. This covers 336 pairs per mode. Check custom end content separately.

accessibility.name: Visible control boundary
accessibility.description: The button edge needs 3:1 contrast only when users need it to see the control. A text-only button can rely on its label.

accessibility.name: Keyboard focus indicator
accessibility.description: The focus outline needs at least 3:1 contrast with the area around the button. Check every style. Destructive buttons use a red outline.

accessibility.name: Disabled appearance
accessibility.description: Disabled controls do not need to meet these contrast ratios.

bestPractices.description: Group buttons that perform related actions on the same object, like copy, cut, paste on selected text.
Use the same variant for all buttons in a group so they look like a single connected unit.
Keep groups small (2–4 buttons). For more actions, use a Toolbar or DropdownMenu instead.
Don't mix wildly different actions. A Save button next to a Delete button in the same group is confusing.
Don't use ButtonGroup for navigation. Use SegmentedControl or TabList for switching between views.
Don't nest ButtonGroups. If you need multiple groups, place them side by side with a gap.
Name the group for what its buttons act on. The label is the group's accessible name and a screen reader reads it before each member.

Keep the group a single Tab stop. Arrow keys move between members along the orientation, Home/End jump to the ends, and disabled members are skipped. This is the WAI-ARIA APG roving tabindex technique: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex

Don't disable the group to show that an action is in flight. A disabled member drops focus, so a keyboard user loses their place; leave the group enabled and show progress on the button that started the work.

组内所有按钮使用相同的变体，使其看起来像一个连接的整体。
保持组较小（2-4 个按钮）。更多操作请使用工具栏或下拉菜单。
不要混合差异很大的操作，将保存按钮和删除按钮放在同一组中会令人困惑。
不要使用 ButtonGroup 进行导航，使用 SegmentedControl 或 TabList 切换视图。
不要嵌套 ButtonGroup。如需多个组，请并排放置并留有间隔。
按钮组的标签应说明这些按钮作用于什么。该标签是按钮组的无障碍名称，屏幕阅读器会在每个成员之前朗读它。
按钮组是单个 Tab 停靠点。方向键沿排列方向在成员间移动焦点，Home/End 跳到首尾，禁用成员会被跳过——即 WAI-ARIA APG 的 roving tabindex 技术。
不要用禁用整个按钮组来表示操作进行中。禁用的成员会失去焦点，键盘用户会丢失位置；请保持按钮组可用，并在发起操作的按钮上显示进度。

usage.description: Calendar lets the user pick a date or date range from a month grid. Use it in booking flows, scheduling UIs, date filters, or anywhere the user needs to see surrounding dates for context.

bestPractices.description: Set min and max dates to limit selection to a valid window, like only future dates for a booking or the current quarter for a report.
Use range mode when the user needs to pick a start and end date, like a trip or a time-off request.
Use dateConstraints to disable specific dates like weekends or holidays, and explain why they are unavailable.
Show two months side by side when the user frequently selects dates that span a month boundary.
Use a calendar for dates far in the past or future like a birth date. A text input is faster for open-ended entry.
Disable large blocks of dates without context. The user should understand why dates are unavailable.

usage.description: Card is a bordered, elevated container for discrete, self-contained items: things you could reorder, remove, or interact with independently. Cards are NOT the default layout tool. Most content groups don't need a container at all; spacing and alignment create visual grouping naturally. Only reach for a Card when items need clear interaction boundaries or visual comparison in a grid.

bestPractices.description: Ask "could I reorder or remove this independently?" If yes, it's a card. If no, it's just a section of the page: use a heading + Stack or Section.
Use cards for discrete items: a single user profile, a single notification, a single metric, a product in a grid. Each card represents one "thing" with clear interaction boundaries.
Spacing and alignment alone create visual grouping. Not everything needs a container; try removing the card and see if the grouping is still clear from whitespace and typography.
Keep padding consistent across sibling cards so they align visually in a grid or list.
Pair a card with Layout when you need a structured header, scrollable content, and footer with actions.

Let cards share a row or grid on a phone: a card shrinks to fit its track and clips content that cannot wrap at its edge. Truncate long IDs, hashes, and URLs with Text maxLines={1} (the full value shows in a tooltip), and give wide content its own scroll region: Table scrolls by itself; put code or other wide content in a ScrollableArea.
Default to cards for visual grouping. A heading + Stack with proper spacing creates hierarchy without adding borders everywhere. Cards should be the exception, not the default.
Wrap page sections in cards. "General Settings", "Notification Preferences", form groups: these are page regions, use Section or heading + stack.
Create identical card grids (icon + heading + text, repeated). Vary the layout or question whether cards are needed at all.
Nest cards inside other cards; flatten the hierarchy or use spacing and dividers instead.
Use color variants for status; use Banner or Badge for that. Color cards are for categorization.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The outer box with border, background, border-radius, and padding.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Any children rendered inside the card. Often a stack of heading, text, and actions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the card (number = pixels, string = used as-is). In a flex row or grid track this is the preferred width: the card shrinks below it when the row is narrower. To hold the width in a flex row, wrap the card in StackItem (static by default) and let the row wrap or scroll. In Grid, set a consumer minWidth on the Card and size the track accordingly.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the card (number = pixels, string = used as-is).

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the card.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the card.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render inside the card.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding using the spacing scale. Omit it and the card takes the theme's card padding rather than a step, so passing a step is a decision to override the theme, not a way to restate the default.
props.default: the theme's card padding (spacing step 4 with no theme)

props.name: variant
props.description: Background color variant. `default` uses the standard card background. `transparent` drops the background entirely. `muted` uses the muted background for de-emphasised cards. The non-semantic variants use the corresponding `--color-background-<name>` token.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. `none` is flat; `low`/`med`/`high` map to the shadow token scale. Raise a card only when it needs to float above surrounding content.

usage.description: Carousel scrolls a row of items horizontally when they overflow the available width. Use it for card grids, image galleries, product lists, or any set of items that should be browsable without taking up the full page.

bestPractices.description: Enable scroll-snap when each item should land precisely at the start edge, like a gallery or product list.
Reach for hasLoop on small, cyclable sets like a photo gallery, where wrapping past the last item back to the first feels natural.
Always provide an aria-label that describes what the carousel contains, like "Featured products" or "Team members".

Carousel implements the WAI-ARIA APG carousel pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) without auto-rotation: the region is labelled and carries aria-roledescription="carousel", each item is a group named "Slide N of M", and the scroll container is a tab stop while its content overflows, so keyboard users can pan it with the arrow keys; while everything fits it stays out of the tab order.
Use a consistent gap and item width so the carousel looks intentional, not like content overflowing by accident.
Trust the built-in navigation: trackpad users can swipe horizontally, and mouse users can hold Shift while scrolling the wheel to move through items.
Use a carousel for content every user must see. Not everyone scrolls horizontally, so put critical content above the fold.
Auto-advance items. Let the user scroll at their own pace.
Nest carousels. A carousel inside a carousel is confusing and breaks keyboard navigation.

anatomy.name: Scroll container
anatomy.description: The horizontal overflow area that holds all items.

anatomy.name: Items
anatomy.description: The children rendered in a row inside the scroll container. With hasSnap, each item snaps to the start edge.

anatomy.name: Fade edges
anatomy.description: Gradient fades on the left and right edges that indicate more content is available. Enabled by default, disable with hasEdgeFade={false}.

anatomy.name: Navigation buttons
anatomy.description: Prev/next buttons that appear when the content can scroll in that direction. Enabled by default, disable with hasButtons={false}.

props.name: children
props.description: Carousel items rendered in a horizontal scroll container.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between items using the spacing token scale.

props.name: hasButtons
props.description: Show prev/next navigation buttons when content is scrollable.

props.name: hasEdgeFade
props.description: Show a gradient edge-fade mask when content overflows, signalling that more items exist off-screen.

props.name: hasLoop
props.description: Wrap-around scrolling: next at the end scrolls to the start, prev at the start scrolls to the end. Buttons stay visible at both edges. Only engages when content overflows.

props.name: hasSnap
props.description: Enable scroll-snap so each child snaps to the start edge.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inline padding inside the scroll container, with matching scroll-padding so snap points align to the content edge.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the carousel region.

props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

usage.description: Carousel 在项目超出可用宽度时将一行项目水平滚动。适用于卡片网格、图片画廊、产品列表，或任何希望无需占据整页即可浏览的项目集合。

bestPractices.description: 当每个项目应精确对齐到起始边缘时启用滚动吸附，例如画廊或产品列表。
在小型可循环的集合（如照片画廊）上使用 hasLoop，此时从最后一项绕回第一项的滚动更自然。
始终提供描述轮播内容的 aria-label，例如"精选产品"或"团队成员"。
Carousel 实现不含自动轮播的 WAI-ARIA APG carousel 模式（https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/）：区域带有标签和 aria-roledescription="carousel"，每个项目是名为“第 N 张，共 M 张”的 group，滚动容器可获得焦点，键盘用户可用方向键平移。
使用一致的间距和项目宽度，让轮播看起来是有意为之，而不是内容意外溢出。
信任内置导航：触控板用户可水平滑动，鼠标用户可按住 Shift 滚动滚轮来浏览项目。
将每位用户都必须看到的内容放入轮播。并非所有人都会水平滚动，关键内容应放在首屏。
自动轮播项目。让用户按自己的节奏滚动。
嵌套轮播。轮播中嵌套轮播会造成困惑并破坏键盘导航。

usage.description: Carousel scrolls items horizontally when they overflow. Use for card grids, galleries, product lists.

bestPractices.description: Enable scroll-snap when each item should land precisely at the start edge: gallery, product list.
Reach for hasLoop on small cyclable sets (photo gallery) where wrapping past the last item back to the first feels natural.
Always provide an aria-label describing what the carousel contains: "Featured products", "Team members".
Use consistent gap + item width so the carousel looks intentional, not like content overflowing by accident.
Trust built-in navigation: trackpad users swipe horizontally, mouse users hold Shift + wheel to move through items.
Use a carousel for content every user must see. Not everyone scrolls horizontally, so put critical content above the fold.
Auto-advance items. Let the user scroll at their own pace.
Nest carousels. A carousel inside a carousel is confusing and breaks keyboard navigation.

usage.description: Center aligns content to the middle of its container. Use it for empty states, loading screens, login forms, or any content that should sit in the center of the available space.

bestPractices.description: Use a single-axis value only in horizontal writing, or after verifying the active writing mode. In vertical writing, the current implementation follows flex main/cross axes rather than the physical prop names.
In horizontal writing, give Center height when using axis="vertical"; centering needs available space on the selected flex axis.
Use isInline to center small elements like icons or badges within a line of text without breaking the text flow.
Keep semantic structure and accessible names on the content. Center is a layout-only container and does not add a role or label.
Wrap large page sections in Center. Use Layout or AppShell for page-level structure.
Use Center for horizontal lists of items. Use Stack with hAlign="center" instead.

components.name: ChatComposer
components.description: Layout shell for a chat composer. Arranges named slots (drawer, header, input, footer, send) with page-radius container, elevation, a keyboard-only editor focus ring, and concentric inner radius for child elements.

usage.description: ChatComposer is the message-entry shell for a chat surface. It coordinates a controlled or uncontrolled draft, provides a default token-capable input and send/stop action, and arranges optional drawer, header, footer, and status content. Custom inputs and send controls can join the same value, submission, disabled, stop, and focus contract through useChatComposerContext().

anatomy.description: Outer composition root that groups the body with an optional status message above or below it.

anatomy.name: Composer body
anatomy.description: Rounded, elevated surface containing the header, input, and footer.

anatomy.name: Drawer
anatomy.description: Content before the body for attachments or other expandable context, typically ChatComposerDrawer.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: Row for start-aligned actions and end-aligned contextual information.

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: Default ChatComposerInput or a custom editor connected through useChatComposerContext().

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Row for caller-supplied footer and send actions plus the primary action.

anatomy.name: Send or stop action
anatomy.description: Default ChatSendButton or a custom sendButton; it submits the current draft or requests interruption.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: Error or warning feedback rendered before or after the composer body.

props.description: Resting elevation of the composer body. `low` (the default) keeps today's raised look: low at rest, bumping to med on hover / focus. `none` flattens it and draws a border. Keyboard focus in the editor adds the shared focus ring in either presentation; pointer focus does not add that ring.

props.description: Slot: left-aligned header actions (attach, mention buttons). Use icon-only size="sm" buttons.

Use ChatComposerInput for trigger menus/tokens, or wire any input (plain textarea, rich editor) to the composition contract via useChatComposerContext(): read value/onChange/onSubmit/canSend and register a focus control on inputControlRef so body-click-to-focus works.

props.description: Where to render the status.

components.name: ChatComposerDrawer
components.description: Collapsible drawer panel that sits above the chat input inside ChatComposer. Pass it to the composer's `drawer` slot to show attachments, context chips, or any supplementary content. When `count` is provided the drawer gains a collapse toggle: collapsed state shows the default Badge and label or caller-provided `collapsedSummary`, while expanded state shows all children.

usage.description: Use ChatComposerDrawer in the ChatComposer drawer slot for supplementary content such as attachments, context chips, or previews. Provide count only when people should be able to collapse that content.

components.name: ChatComposerInput
components.description: Rich text input for the chat composer. Supports trigger menus (type @ or / to open a typeahead), inline tokens rendered as badges, message history recall with ArrowUp/Down, paste/drop file handling, and a 16px iOS font-size floor to prevent input zoom. Pass it to ChatComposer's input slot when you need more than a plain textarea.

usage.description: Pass ChatComposerInput to ChatComposer's input slot when the draft needs trigger menus, inline tokens, history recall, dictation insertion, or file intake.

bestPractices.description: Use handleRef for programmatic text or token insertion; inserted text follows the same onChange pipeline as typing.
Use onFiles for files pasted or dropped onto the editor, and keep file validation and upload progress in the product layer.
Use custom token rendering for ordinary mentions or commands; prefer the structured badge form so tokens remain predictable and themeable.

anatomy.description: The themed container that forwards the root ref and BaseProps styling seams.

anatomy.name: Editable surface
anatomy.description: The labeled contenteditable textbox or combobox that owns text, selection, keyboard, paste, and drop behavior.

anatomy.description: Visual guidance shown only while the serialized draft is empty.
