templates.name: Popover — Confirm Action
templates.description: Inline confirmation popover for destructive actions with delete and cancel buttons.

templates.name: Popover — Filter Panel
templates.description: Popover with checkbox filters and apply/reset actions.

templates.name: usePopover — Quick Actions
templates.description: Custom quick-actions popover using usePopover for trigger refs, ARIA attributes, and focus trapping.

templates.name: Popover — Keyboard Shortcuts
templates.description: Popover displaying a list of keyboard shortcuts with key and description pairs.

templates.name: Popover — Settings Panel
templates.description: Popover with toggle switches for managing user preferences like notifications, dark mode, and sounds.

templates.name: PowerSearch — Content Search
templates.description: Power search with contentSearchFieldKey so free-text input maps to a title field automatically.

templates.name: PowerSearch — Full Featured
templates.description: Power search with multiple field types: enum, multi-select, entity, and text filters.

templates.name: PowerSearch — Preset Filters
templates.description: Power search initialized with pre-set filter tokens for status and priority.

templates.name: PowerSearch — Search with Table
templates.description: Composition of PowerSearch with Table using usePowerSearchConfig to auto-generate config and filter data.

templates.name: PowerSearch
templates.description: Token-based filter bar with enum and text fields, pre-populated with sample filters.

templates.name: Product Detail
templates.description: Single-item detail pairing a media gallery with a selection column: variant swatches, a quantity stepper, primary and secondary commit actions, and collapsible specification sections below.

templates.name: Product Gallery
templates.description: Uniform card grid where every tile carries media, title, supporting line, and a price. Browse-to-select only, with no filtering and no detail surface.

templates.name: ProgressBar — Custom Format
templates.description: Progress bar with a custom value label showing disk usage in GB.

templates.name: ProgressBar — Indeterminate
templates.description: Indeterminate progress bar for operations with unknown duration.

templates.name: ProgressBar — Semantic Variants
templates.description: All semantic color variants stacked vertically.

templates.name: ProgressBar
templates.description: A progress bar filled to 60%.

templates.name: ProgressBar — With Value Label
templates.description: Progress bar with its current percentage displayed.

templates.name: RadioList — Horizontal Layout
templates.description: Radio list with horizontal orientation for compact selections.

templates.name: RadioListItem — Basic
templates.description: Radio items with labels and descriptions inside a controlled RadioList. Use for single-choice option groups like shipping methods.

templates.name: RadioListItem
templates.description: Radio list items with labels, descriptions, and different states including disabled.

templates.name: RadioList — Pricing Tier
templates.description: Radio list with pricing info in end content for plan selection.

templates.name: RadioList — With Descriptions
templates.description: Radio list with descriptions on the group and each item.

templates.name: RadioList — With Validation
templates.description: Required radio list with an error message when nothing is selected.

templates.description: A collapsible sidebar with snap points, driven by useResizable. Dragging snaps to preset widths, dragging past the minimum collapses the panel, and the expand method restores it programmatically.

templates.description: axis="inline" scrolls the same cards sideways; isFullBleed lets the rail run to the panel edges while the content padding keeps the first card aligned with the heading.

templates.description: axis="both" gives the content box max-content inline sizing, so a board wider and taller than its panel scrolls on both axes from one viewport.

templates.name: Section — Variants

templates.name: Section — Default with Wash

templates.name: Section — With Dividers

templates.name: SegmentedControl — Disabled Item
templates.description: Segmented control with an individually disabled option for unavailable choices.

templates.name: SegmentedControl — Fill Layout
templates.description: Segmented control that stretches segments equally to fill the available width, useful for fixed-width containers.

templates.name: SegmentedControl — Icon Only
templates.description: Compact segmented control with hidden labels, showing only icons for space-constrained layouts.

templates.name: SegmentedControlItem — Basic
templates.description: A row of label-only options that switches between a few views, here Board, List, and Timeline. Each item declares a value; the parent control holds the selected value and change handler.

templates.name: SegmentedControl — With Icons
templates.description: Segmented control with icon and label pairs for a view mode switcher.

templates.name: SelectableCard — Elevated
templates.description: Raised selectable cards with `elevation="low"`. The inset selection ring composes on top of the shadow, so a selected card keeps its elevation.

templates.name: Selector — Clearable
templates.description: Selector with a clear button to reset the selected value.

templates.name: Selector — Ghost Toolbar
templates.description: Borderless Selector variant composed with ghost buttons in a toolbar.

templates.name: SelectorOption

templates.name: Selector — Grouped Sections
templates.description: Selector with options grouped into labeled sections.

templates.name: Selector — Validation States

templates.name: SideNav — End Content

templates.description: Demonstrates SideNavHeading with an app name, logo icon, superheading, and subheading.

templates.description: Navigation links inside a SideNav, each with a label, an icon, and an href. Mark the item for the current page with isSelected.

templates.name: SideNavItem
templates.description: Demonstrates SideNavItem with selected, icon, disabled, and nested states.

templates.name: SideNav — Nested Items
templates.description: Side navigation with collapsible nested items for settings or hierarchical menus.

templates.name: SideNavSection — Basic
templates.description: Group related SideNavItems under titled sections. Use sections to organize longer navigation lists into scannable clusters like Overview and Account.

templates.name: SideNavSection
templates.description: Demonstrates SideNavSection with titled groups of navigation items.

templates.name: SideNav — Header with Menu
templates.description: Side navigation with an account switcher dropdown in the header for multi-account apps.

templates.name: Skeleton — Card Loading
templates.description: Card skeleton with avatar, name, and content lines.

templates.name: Skeleton
templates.description: A skeleton loading placeholder.

templates.name: Skeleton — Staggered List
templates.description: Staggered skeleton lines with varying widths.

templates.name: Skeleton — Table Rows
templates.description: Table skeleton with staggered column widths.

templates.name: Slider — Formatted Value
templates.description: Slider with custom formatting showing temperature in Fahrenheit.

templates.name: Slider — Range
templates.description: Range slider for selecting a value range like price bounds.

templates.name: Slider
templates.description: A slider control set to 50%.

templates.name: Slider — With Marks
templates.description: Slider with labeled tick marks at fixed intervals.

templates.name: Slider — Validation States
templates.description: Sliders with error, warning, and success validation states.

templates.name: Spinner — On Media Shade
templates.description: Default and onMedia shade spinners for light and dark backgrounds.

templates.name: Spinner
templates.description: A large spinner indicator.

templates.name: Spinner — Sizes
templates.description: All spinner sizes displayed side by side.

templates.name: Spinner — With Label
templates.description: Spinners with text and rich multi-line labels.

templates.name: Stack — Alignment
templates.description: Buttons positioned at the start, center, and end of a row.

templates.name: Stack — Directions
templates.description: Badges arranged horizontally and vertically in side-by-side cards.

templates.name: Stack — Fill Item
templates.description: An avatar, text, and button in a row; the text stretches to fill the available space.

templates.name: StackItem — Fill
templates.description: A static-width item next to one that fills the remaining space. Wrap stack children in StackItem when an item needs explicit sizing control.

templates.name: StackItem
templates.description: StackItem can be used within HStack or VStack for more granular control over individual item sizing and alignment, but is optional; stack children work without it.

templates.name: StatusDot — Pulsing
templates.description: Animated pulsing dots for live, processing, and error states.

templates.name: StatusDot
templates.description: A positive status dot indicator.

templates.name: StatusDot — Status Indicators
templates.description: Labeled status dot list for presence indicators like online, away, and offline.

templates.name: StatusDot — Variants
templates.description: All five semantic color variants displayed in a row.

templates.name: Step — Content Slot
templates.description: Children passed to a Step render below its description, indented to line up with the label rather than the indicator, and stay outside the clickable label area so buttons inside remain their own targets. In a full flow you gate the slot on the step being active. That is what turns a vertical stepper into an expanding one.

templates.name: Step — Indicator
templates.description: Everything the indicator prop accepts: the auto default, an always-number badge, a custom ReactNode, and none, each on its own completed Step so the prop is the only difference between them. Every variant occupies the same 16px box, so a step swapping its number for a check as it completes never shifts the label beside it. The last cell shows that a custom node can be live rather than static: a Spinner on a step that is in progress, shaded `inherit` so it picks up the step's own tint like any other glyph.

templates.name: Stepper — Custom Content
templates.description: A vertical stepper where each step owns a slice of the page. The content slot takes any node (form fields, a summary panel, a banner), so a stepper is not limited to multi-step forms. Rendering the slot only for the active step is what makes the flow expand one step at a time.

templates.name: Stepper — Indicator Modes
templates.description: The indicator prop side by side: none (the bar and label carry the progress on their own), auto (check when done, ring when current, number ahead), always-number, and a custom icon per step.

templates.name: Stepper — On-Track Horizontal
templates.description: The on-track layout in horizontal orientation: instead of sitting beside the label, each indicator is slotted into the connector itself, so the numbered nodes read as beads on one continuous line. Labels center under their node.

templates.name: Stepper — On-Track Vertical
templates.description: The on-track layout in vertical orientation: indicators sit inline on a continuous connector rail, with each label and description beside its node. Compare with the separated layout, where the indicator sits alongside its own bar segment instead of on a shared rail.

templates.name: Stepper — Checkout Progress
templates.description: The default stepper: a horizontal track where every step owns an equal segment of the progress bar above its label. The default auto indicator resolves itself per step: a check once the step is done, a ring on the current step, a number for the ones still ahead. Click any step to jump.

templates.name: Stepper — Validation Status
templates.description: Semantic status per step in a verification flow: success shows a green check, error a red glyph, accent the in-progress step. Status sets the indicator color and glyph only, never the connector, and is announced to assistive tech as text.

templates.name: Stepper — Horizontal Narrow Collapsed
templates.description: A narrow horizontal stepper using horizontalOptions. At 320px wide, four steps fall below the 112px minimumStepWidth and collapse into a current-step summary with Previous and Next controls.

templates.name: Step
templates.description: A single Step, with every part it can render: the indicator, the label with its optional marker and trailing endContent, and the description beneath. A Step never sets its own completed/current state. It declares its index and derives the rest from the parent Stepper, so one Step in one Stepper is a complete example.

templates.name: Step — States
templates.description: Every state a single Step can land in, each shown as one Step in its own Stepper. Completed, current, and upcoming are derived by comparing the step index against the parent activeStep, so they are never set directly; isDisabled and status are the two a step declares itself. Status is a separate axis from progress, which is why a completed step can still carry a warning.

templates.name: useTableStickyColumns — Pinned Columns
templates.description: A Table using useTableStickyColumns to pin the Name column to the start edge and Status to the end edge. Scroll horizontally; pinned columns stay in view with a soft shadow over the scrolling content.

templates.name: Switch — Disabled
templates.description: Disabled switch with label and description for gated features.

templates.name: Switch — Settings Panel
templates.description: Settings panel with spread-spaced switches in a card.

templates.name: Switch
templates.description: A toggle switch for enabling notifications.

templates.name: Switch — With Description
templates.description: Toggle with a label and supporting description text.

templates.name: Switch — With Status
templates.description: Switches with error, warning, and success validation states.

templates.name: SyntaxTheme — Dark Preset
templates.description: Wrap a code block in SyntaxTheme to apply a dark syntax preset such as Dracula.

templates.name: SyntaxTheme — Light Preset
templates.description: Use a light syntax preset for code examples that need to sit on light documentation surfaces.

templates.name: SyntaxTheme — Compact Preset
templates.description: A concise code block rendered with the One Dark Pro syntax preset to show how SyntaxTheme changes highlighting colors without making the page long.

templates.name: Simple Table
templates.description: Flat row collection where columns sort, rows select into a bulk-action toolbar, and each row carries an overflow menu. Sortable but ungrouped, with no detail pane, the baseline shape.

templates.name: Collapsible Table
templates.description: Several tables on one page, each in a collapsible card with its own columns — for groups that do not share a schema, where one table would stand full of empty cells. One time range drives them all, and rows expand into a history chart. Accounts, integrations, sections, sort, expand, or collapse.

templates.name: Comparison Table
templates.description: Transposed matrix that puts candidates in the columns and criteria in grouped rows, with a pinned label column that survives horizontal scroll, columns you can swap or add, and best-in-row marks you can toggle. Compare, comparison, matrix, spec sheet, feature grid, pricing table, benchmark, frozen column, sticky column, or side-by-side.

templates.name: Filterable Table
templates.description: Flat row collection built around progressive filtering: a token bar that escalates into full query syntax, saved views that persist a filter set, column and grouping options, and a resizable detail pane.

templates.name: Grouped Table
templates.description: Row collection bundled into collapsible sections with per-group counts, so a long list reads as a handful of blocks that expand and collapse. Query filtering and a resizable inspector for the selected row.

templates.name: Inbox Table
templates.description: Two-pane message queue: the table indexes a reading pane rather than being the destination, with a divider you drag to resize. Rows stack when the table narrows, not the window; threads read as collapsible messages; replying opens a composer that leaves the list live.

templates.name: Searchable Table
templates.description: Flat table of uniform rows under a block of record-level facts, narrowed three ways at once — a full-text search box, a scope toggle, and per-column popovers — with sortable and filterable columns, per-row hover detail, and totals derived from the visible rows that flag themselves as partial while a filter is on. The shape for one homogeneous list, not nested rows or groups with their own columns.

templates.name: Tree Table
templates.description: Hierarchical table where every parent row rolls up from its children — a code repository whose folders show the newest commit beneath them, beside a detail sidebar and a rendered README. Columns resize, siblings sort within their own level, arrow keys walk the rows, and search prunes the tree to matching branches.

templates.name: Table: Bulk Actions
templates.description: Controlled row selection with the reusable TableSelectionToolbar rendered in flow above the table. Product actions occupy the logical start; synchronized selection count and complete clear action occupy the logical end.

templates.name: Table — Column Settings
templates.description: Table with a column visibility picker in the toolbar. Toggle columns on and off.

templates.name: Table — Popover Filters
templates.description: Table with popover filter controls triggered by icons in column headers.

templates.name: Table: Floating Bulk Actions
templates.description: The reusable TableSelectionToolbar inside a capped, self-contained scroll region for a long non-sticky table below metric cards. The caller-owned sticky placement keeps actions 16px from the example scrollport without moving the table when selection changes.

templates.name: Table — Grid Dividers
templates.description: Compact table with grid dividers showing both row and column borders, suited for dense numeric data.

templates.name: useTableGroupedRows — Collapsible Groups
templates.description: A table grouped into collapsible sections with useTableGroupedRows. Each group gets a full-width header with a chevron, label, and member count; click to collapse/expand.

templates.name: Table — In Card
templates.description: Table composed inside a card with a heading, demonstrating container bleed alignment.

templates.name: Table — Inline Filters
templates.description: Table with inline filter controls rendered directly below each column header.

templates.name: Table — Paginated Data
templates.description: Paginated data table navigating through a larger dataset page by page.

templates.name: Table — Resizable Columns
templates.description: Table with draggable column resize handles. Drag the right edge of any header to resize.

templates.name: Table — Rich Cell Content
templates.description: Table with rich cell content using Link for emails and Badge for role labels.

templates.name: useTableRowExpansion — Tree Table
templates.description: A tree table using useTableRowExpansion with inherited columns. Child rows use the same columns as parents, indented by depth. Click the chevron or right-click to expand/collapse.

templates.name: useTableRowIndex — Numbered Rows
templates.description: A table with a prepended row-number column via useTableRowIndex. Numbering is monospaced, right-aligned, and follows the rendered data order.

templates.name: useTableRowStatus - Semantic and Custom Markers
templates.description: A job table using both row-status paths: status resolves themed semantic glyphs and tones, while color stays a custom paint choice with an optional caller-selected icon or the stable dot.

templates.name: Table — Row Selection
templates.description: Table with row selection checkboxes and a select-all header checkbox.

templates.name: Table
templates.description: Data-driven table with proportional and pixel column widths and hover highlighting.

templates.name: Table — Sortable Columns
templates.description: Table with sortable columns, click headers to sort ascending or descending.

templates.name: Table — Striped Rows
templates.description: Table with alternating row colors and hover highlighting for easy scanning.

templates.name: useTableTreeData: Tree Table
templates.description: A file-tree table built from nested data. useTableTreeState flattens the tree into the visible rows and owns the expanded set; useTableTreeData draws the per-level indent and the expand/collapse chevron in the tree column. The two hooks are designed to work together, so this one example covers both. hasExpandAllControl adds the expand-all/collapse-all toggle to the tree column header. Collapsed branches are unmounted, not hidden.

templates.name: TabList — Fill Layout
templates.description: Tabs that stretch to fill the available width with a bottom divider.

templates.name: TabList — With Actions
templates.description: Page header pattern with tabs on the left and action buttons pushed to the right. When hasDivider is true, match the Button size to the TabList size so the tabs and actions align to a shared baseline above the divider.

templates.name: TabList — With Badge
templates.description: Tabs with notification badge counts rendered via endContent. Uses error variant for urgent counts and neutral for informational ones.

templates.name: TabList — With Icons
templates.description: Tabs with leading icons alongside text labels.

templates.name: TabList — With Overflow Menu
templates.description: Tab list with a dropdown menu for additional items that do not fit inline.

templates.name: TabList — With Status Dot
templates.description: Tabs with status dot indicators rendered via endContent to show live environment health at a glance.

templates.name: TabMenu — Basic
templates.description: An overflow menu at the end of a TabList that collects secondary tabs behind a dropdown. Use it when there are more tabs than fit comfortably inline.

templates.name: TabMenu
templates.description: TabMenu is an overflow menu within a TabList that groups additional tab options into a dropdown, showing the selected option's label as the trigger text.

templates.name: Tab
templates.description: Tab is an individual tab item within a TabList, supporting labels, icons, selected icons, and end content slots.

templates.name: Tab — Selected Icon
templates.description: A tab that changes its icon when selected.

templates.name: TextArea — Character Count
templates.description: Textareas with maxLength and a live character counter. The counter turns red when the limit is exceeded.

templates.name: TextArea
templates.description: A text area with placeholder text.

templates.name: TextArea — States
templates.description: Required, disabled, and loading textareas side by side. Shows the interactive states the component supports.

templates.name: TextArea — Validation
templates.description: All three status variants (error, warning, and success) with status messages, plus error without a message. Use to show inline validation feedback as the user types.

templates.name: TextArea — Icon
templates.description: Textareas with a leading icon that hints at the expected content, like a chat bubble for messages or a pencil for notes.

templates.name: Text — Colors
templates.description: All text color options (primary, secondary, disabled, placeholder, active) applied to body text to show their intended use.

templates.name: Text — Heading Levels
templates.description: All 6 heading levels (h1 through h6) rendered with Heading to show the full type scale.

templates.name: Text — Inline
templates.description: Mixing body and code text inline within a single line using the default inline display mode.

templates.name: TextInput — Icon
templates.description: Inputs with a leading icon that hints at the expected content. Use when the icon helps users identify the field faster, like a lock for passwords or an envelope for email.

templates.name: TextInput — Search
templates.description: Search input with a hidden label, start icon, and clear button. Use for toolbar and header search bars where the icon provides sufficient context.

templates.name: TextInput — Sizes
templates.description: Small, medium, and large inputs side by side. Use small in dense UIs like table filters, medium for most forms, and large for prominent single-field pages.

templates.name: TextInput — States
templates.description: Error, warning, and success validation states with status messages. Use to show users what went wrong and how to fix it.

templates.name: TextInput — Status variant
templates.description: The statusVariant prop controls whether the status message is attached to the bordered input (default, overlapping directly below) or detached from it (floating below as a separate element with spacing).

templates.name: TextInput — Types
templates.description: Text, password, and email types plus field-level features: tooltip, required, optional, description, disabled, and loading.

templates.name: Text — Truncation
templates.description: Single-line and multi-line text truncation with ellipsis using maxLines in a width-constrained container.

templates.name: Text — Types
templates.description: All 5 semantic text types (body, large, label, supporting, code) with their default styling from the theme.

templates.name: Text — Weight
templates.description: The 4 font weight variants (normal, medium, semibold, bold) applied to body text.

templates.name: Text — Word Break
templates.description: Compares break-word and break-all word break modes on a long unbreakable string.

templates.name: Text — Wrap
templates.description: The 4 text-wrap modes (wrap, nowrap, balance, pretty) shown in width-constrained containers.

templates.name: Theme Showcase
templates.description: Several unrelated product surfaces rendered together on one canvas so a token change can be judged across contexts at once. A comparison harness rather than a layout to ship.

templates.name: Theme — Apply Theme
templates.description: Wrap a subtree in Theme to apply a theme to every child component in that region.

templates.name: Theme — Nested Theme
templates.description: Nested Theme providers let a local region use a different theme without affecting the rest of the page.

templates.name: Theme — Distinct Themes
templates.description: Two visually distinct theme providers wrapping identical content to show how Theme changes the visual treatment of child components.

templates.name: Theme — Switch Themes
templates.description: Use state to switch the theme object passed to Theme and preview a different visual treatment.

templates.name: Thumbnail — Disabled
templates.description: Thumbnails in the disabled state with reduced opacity. The open and remove buttons stay focusable and announced as disabled, and call nothing.

templates.name: Thumbnail — Gallery
templates.description: A row of clickable thumbnails with labels that open a detail view. Use for image attachment lists where users need to preview and manage uploads.

templates.name: Thumbnail — Removable
templates.description: Thumbnails with a remove button overlay. The close button uses APCA luminance detection to stay visible on both dark and light images.

templates.name: Thumbnail
templates.description: A thumbnail with an image and label.

templates.name: Thumbnail — States
templates.description: All visual states side by side: image loaded, placeholder, skeleton loading, and upload overlay. Demonstrates the full lifecycle of a thumbnail from empty to loaded.

templates.name: TimeInput — Constrained
templates.description: Time inputs with min/max constraints limiting selection to specific windows. Use to prevent out-of-bounds selections for appointments, reservations, or shift scheduling.

templates.name: TimeInput — Formats
templates.description: 12-hour, 24-hour, and seconds formats side by side. Use 12h for US-centric UIs, 24h for international or technical contexts, and seconds for precise timing.

templates.name: TimeInput — Increment
templates.description: Time input with a custom step increment. Arrow keys jump by the specified interval (e.g. 15 minutes) for quick slot-based scheduling.

templates.name: TimeInput
templates.description: A time input that uses the browser/OS picker on touch by default and Astryx typed entry on fine pointers.

templates.name: TimeInput — States
templates.description: Default, disabled, error, warning, and success states. Use status messages to give users clear feedback about their time selection.

templates.name: Timer — Formats
templates.description: Elapsed compact units and stopwatch clock notation shown from the same start time.

templates.name: Timer — Inline
templates.description: A Timer composed into status copy while inheriting the surrounding typography.

templates.name: Timer — Typography
templates.description: Timer using its Timestamp-matched default typography and an emphasized override.

templates.name: Timestamp — Auto
templates.description: Auto format that shows relative time for recent dates and switches to the full date for older ones. The default choice for most use cases.

templates.name: Timestamp — Colors
templates.description: Timestamp rendered in each available color variant: primary, secondary, disabled, and active.

templates.name: Timestamp — Formats
templates.description: All display formats side by side: date, date_time, time, and their system equivalents. Use date and date_time for user-facing UI, system variants for logs and dev tools.

templates.name: Timestamp — Relative
templates.description: Relative time labels from seconds to months ago, with hover tooltips showing the full date. Use in feeds, comment threads, and activity logs.

templates.name: Timestamp — Timezone
templates.description: Timestamps with the timezone abbreviation appended. Enable isTimezoneShown for audiences across time zones, like audit logs or team calendars.

templates.name: Timestamp — Tooltip time zones
templates.description: Hover tooltips that show one instant across several time zones or formats. Use tooltipEntries when readers must compare zones, like an incident log carrying both the reader's time and the event's origin zone.

templates.name: Toast — Action
templates.description: Persistent toasts with a trailing button or link so the user can act on the notification, like undoing a delete or viewing a report.

templates.name: Toast — Deduplication
templates.description: Prevent duplicate toasts with uniqueID. Use ignore to keep the first toast, or overwrite to replace it with updated content like a progress percentage.

templates.name: Toast — Dismiss
templates.description: Show a persistent toast and dismiss it programmatically using the function returned by useToast. Use for long-running operations that need manual cleanup.

templates.name: Toast
templates.description: Imperative toast notifications triggered with useToast and rendered in the toast viewport.

templates.name: Toast — Stacking
templates.description: Multiple toasts stacking vertically with smooth enter and exit animations. Click repeatedly to see how toasts queue and dismiss.

templates.name: Toast — Types
templates.description: Info and error toast variants side by side. Info toasts auto-dismiss after 5 seconds, error toasts persist until the user dismisses them.

templates.name: ToggleButton — Color
templates.description: Toggle buttons with colored icons in the pressed state. Shows accent-colored toolbar formatting and semantic reaction colors (yellow star, red heart, blue bookmark).

templates.name: ToggleButton — Group
templates.description: Toggle button groups in single-select and multi-select modes. Single selection acts as a view mode switcher; multiple selection forms a formatting toolbar.

templates.name: ToggleButtonGroup
templates.description: ToggleButtonGroup manages a set of ToggleButtons with single-select or multi-select behavior for options like view modes or filters.

templates.name: ToggleButtonGroup — Vertical
templates.description: A vertically stacked ToggleButtonGroup using the vertical orientation, shown with both single-select and multi-select behavior, ideal for sidebar-style option lists and vertical toolbars.

templates.name: ToggleButton — Icon Swap
templates.description: Icon-only toggle buttons that swap between outline and solid icons when pressed. Use for actions like favorite, bookmark, or mute where the icon itself communicates the state.

templates.name: ToggleButton — Label
templates.description: Toggle buttons with visible text labels that show a font weight shift on press. Use when the icon alone is not enough to communicate the action.

templates.name: ToggleButton — States
templates.description: Default, pressed, disabled, and loading states of a standalone toggle button. Shows how visual treatment changes across states.

templates.name: Token — Clickable
templates.description: Interactive tokens that respond to clicks. Use for toggleable filters or tokens that open a detail view when selected.

templates.name: Token — Colors
templates.description: All 11 color variants in default and disabled states. Use color to categorize entities or convey status at a glance.

templates.name: Token — End Content
templates.description: Tokens with trailing content like a count badge or status indicator after the label. Use for notification counts, item quantities, or compact status info.

templates.name: Token — Icon
templates.description: Tokens with a leading icon that identifies the entity type. Use when the icon helps users recognize the token category faster, like a user icon for people or a tag icon for labels.

templates.name: Tokenizer — Clear
templates.description: Tokenizer with a built-in clear-all button for bulk removal of all selected tokens.

templates.name: Tokenizer — Creatable
templates.description: Free-text tokenizer for creating custom tags and a combined create-or-search pattern. Use when users need to enter values that may not exist in a predefined list.

templates.name: Tokenizer — End Content
templates.description: Tokenizer with an action button in the end slot. Use for inline actions like applying selections alongside the input.

templates.name: Tokenizer — Icon
templates.description: Tokenizer with a leading search icon to visually reinforce the search behavior.

templates.name: Tokenizer — Max Entries
templates.description: Tokenizer with a maximum selection limit. The input hides automatically when the limit is reached, preventing further additions.

templates.name: Tokenizer — Overflow
templates.description: Tokenizer with overflow truncation when unfocused. Inline mode pushes content down on expand; layer mode overlays without shifting layout.

templates.name: Tokenizer
templates.description: A tokenizer with preset tags and search source.

templates.name: Tokenizer — States
templates.description: Tokenizer in disabled, error, warning, and success states. Use to communicate validation feedback or lock a selection from editing.

templates.name: Token — Removable
templates.description: Tokens with a dismiss button for selections the user can undo. Use in multi-select fields, active filters, or any list of user-chosen items.

templates.name: Toolbar — Bulk Actions
templates.description: A compact toolbar with the muted variant for showing bulk selection actions. Use when the user selects multiple items in a list or table and needs quick access to batch operations.

templates.name: Toolbar — Card Header
templates.description: A toolbar as a card header with a left-aligned title and icon actions on the right. Use Toolbar instead of LayoutHeader when your card header has interactive actions; Toolbar adds start/end slot layout, keyboard navigation, and automatic size cascading. If the header is just a title with no actions, a LayoutHeader or Section is enough.

templates.name: Toolbar — Sizes
templates.description: Small, medium, and large toolbars side by side. The size prop cascades to child buttons and inputs automatically. Use small in dense UIs like cards, medium for most cases, and large for spacious layouts.

templates.name: Toolbar — Table Filter
templates.description: Filter bar above a table: a search box leads the row, each field beside it is a closed trigger that doubles as its own filter chip — the bare field name unset, the whole clause once set — and the clauses fold from the end into a count as the row narrows, followed by a live result count, a clear all, and a column picker. Use to search, filter, and narrow flat rows of records such as jobs, orders, tickets, or users.

templates.name: Toolbar — Three Slot
templates.description: A toolbar with start, center, and end content using the three-column grid layout. Use when you need a centered title or heading with navigation and actions on either side.

templates.name: Toolbar — Tab Navigation
templates.description: A toolbar with tabs in the start slot and an action button at the end. Use as a card or section header when content is split into tabs with a primary action alongside.

templates.name: Tooltip — Action Bar
templates.description: Tooltips on an action button bar with contextual descriptions.

templates.name: Tooltip — Hook Usage
templates.description: Tooltip using the useTooltip hook for programmatic control.

templates.name: Tooltip — Inline Text
templates.description: Tooltips on inline text terms for definitions.

templates.name: TopNav — Centered Navigation
templates.description: Navigation layout with center-aligned nav items flanked by a logo heading and end actions.

templates.name: TopNav — Enterprise Dashboard
templates.description: Full-featured navigation bar with icon-labeled nav items, search, notifications, and a primary CTA.

templates.name: TopNavHeading — Basic
templates.description: A product heading with a logo inside a TopNav, linked to the home page. Use as the leading brand element of a top navigation bar.

templates.name: TopNavHeading
templates.description: Demonstrates TopNavHeading with a logo and text, both as a plain display and as a clickable link.

templates.name: TopNav — Hover Menu
templates.description: Navigation bar with a hover-triggered dropdown menu showing product items with icons and descriptions.

templates.name: TopNavItem — Basic
templates.description: Navigation links inside a TopNav with one item marked as selected. Use for top-level pages of an application.

templates.name: TopNavItem
templates.description: Demonstrates TopNavItem with selected, icon, disabled, and default states.

templates.name: TopNav — Mega Menu
templates.description: Marketing-style navigation with a full-width mega menu featuring product items and a promotional featured card.

templates.name: TopNavMegaMenu — Basic
templates.description: A mega menu trigger inside a TopNav that opens a panel of rich link items. Use when a navigation section has multiple destinations worth describing.

templates.name: TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard — Basic
templates.description: A promotional card with a title, description, and call-to-action link. Pass it to the featured slot of a TopNavMegaMenu to highlight announcements.

templates.name: TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard
templates.description: Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard with a title, description, and CTA link inside a mega menu.

templates.name: TopNavMegaMenuItem — Basic
templates.description: Rich link items with an icon, title, and description. Use inside the items slot of a TopNavMegaMenu to describe each destination.

templates.name: TopNavMegaMenuItem
templates.description: Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenuItem with icons, titles, and descriptions inside a mega menu.

templates.name: TopNavMegaMenu
templates.description: Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenu with items and a featured card in the mega menu panel.

templates.name: TopNavMenu — Basic
templates.description: A dropdown menu inside a TopNav built from an items array with icons and descriptions. Use to group related destinations under a single trigger.

templates.name: TopNavMenu
templates.description: Demonstrates TopNavMenu with a hover-triggered dropdown containing items with icons and descriptions.

templates.name: TopNav — Multiple Dropdowns
templates.description: Navigation bar with multiple hover-triggered dropdown menus that auto-close when switching between them.

templates.name: TopNav — With Logo
templates.description: Navigation bar with a branded logo icon, heading link, nav items, and a profile action.

templates.name: TreeList — File Tree With Icons
templates.description: File browser tree with folder and document icons distinguishing directories from files.

templates.name: TreeList — Interactive Settings

params.name: options.containerRef
params.description: The area the glide stays inside: the ref you already give your scroll container or panel. A ScrollableArea ref reaches its native scroll viewport, so pass that.

returns.name: animatedLayout
returns.description: An opaque handle with no public members. Pass it to the animatedLayout prop of a component whose size changes, such as TreeList or Collapsible.

usage.description: Returns a handle to pass to a component whose size changes, such as TreeList or Collapsible. When that component changes size, it and the content after it inside `containerRef` animate together on one shared motion role. Fixed and stuck sticky elements stay put, the glide never scrolls the area, and Reduce Motion is respected. It applies under every pointer, a mouse included. Without the handle a component keeps its jump: content after it takes its place at once. Content after the change may mix Astryx components and your own elements; none of it opts in.

bestPractices.description: Create one handle per scroll container or panel and pass the same handle to every component in it whose size changes.
Pass the ref you already give ScrollableArea as containerRef; ScrollableArea does not register itself.
Wrap the content after a disclosure in an extra element to make it move; everything after the change inside the container moves on its own.
Animate height yourself alongside it; the glide moves content with a compositor translate and never animates height.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.hasReplace
params.description: The instance states one current state, such as a search's result count: each message it writes withdraws the instance's previous message while that one has not been spoken yet, whatever their politeness, and is spoken at its own politeness. A message already spoken stays. Messages from other instances, and from instances without hasReplace, still join. Give each state a component reports its own instance, for example one for the result count and one for selection changes.

returns.name: announce
returns.description: Speaks a message through the live region the caller can be heard from: the shared one on the page body, or, when the calling component is rendered inside an open Astryx modal (Dialog, modal BottomSheet, modal Drawer, Lightbox, MobileNav, CommandPalette), a persistent region inside that modal, since a native modal hides the page-body region from assistive technology. Politeness defaults to "polite"; messages announced in the same frame are joined, in order, into one announcement, and an identical repeat is kept once, except that each message from a hasReplace instance replaces the previous message of that instance not yet spoken. An empty message clears any lingering status, including joined messages not yet spoken, instead of announcing.

usage.description: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.

bestPractices.description: Reach for this instead of hand-rolling an aria-live div; a region rendered with its content usually does not announce at all.
Keep "polite" for status and result counts; reserve "assertive" for errors and time-sensitive alerts, since it interrupts whatever the screen reader is saying.
Announce the outcome, not the interaction; "12 results" rather than "search ran".
Send a value that keeps changing, such as a result count as the user types, through its own useAnnounce({hasReplace: true}) instance, so input faster than a frame says only the latest count.
Announce content that is already visible and correctly labeled in the DOM; that doubles up for screen reader users.

bestPractices.description: Attach both onClick and onMouseUp to the container element for full click handling including middle-click.
Use inside ClickableCard or SelectableCard for the standard card interaction pattern.
Use when the entire container is a single interactive element; just use a <button> or <a> directly.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.announce
params.description: Message announced to a polite live region on a successful copy. A swapped aria-label alone is not reliably announced, so pass the localized confirmation (e.g. "Copied") to have it spoken. Omit to skip the announcement.

params.name: options.resetAfterMs
params.description: Milliseconds isCopied stays true after a successful copy before reverting.

returns.name: copy
returns.description: Writes text to the clipboard. On success flips isCopied to true, announces the configured message, restarts the reset timer, and resolves true. A clipboard rejection is a silent no-op that leaves the copied state unchanged and resolves false.

returns.name: isCopied
returns.description: True for resetAfterMs after the most recent successful copy, then reverts. Drive the copied confirmation (e.g. a copy → check icon flip) off this.

usage.description: Copy-to-clipboard behavior: the clipboard write, a transient isCopied flag with its own reset timer, and an optional polite screen-reader announcement. Extracted so every copy affordance is a thin control over one implementation instead of re-deriving the timer and announcement. Rapid re-copies restart the reset timer so the confirmation always lasts the full duration, and the timer is cleaned up on unmount. CodeBlock and Timestamp build their built-in copy buttons on it; reach for it directly when building a copy affordance that is not a plain icon button (a menu item, a labeled text button, a copy-on-click value chip).

bestPractices.description: Drive the copied confirmation (copy → check icon, label swap) off the returned isCopied flag rather than tracking your own state.
Pass a localized announce message so the copy is spoken by screen readers; swapping the button aria-label alone is not reliably announced.
For the common compact icon copy button, render a ghost IconButton with a "Copy" tooltip and wire onClick to copy(); the tooltip stays "Copy" and the icon flip is the confirmation.
Track a separate copied useState alongside the hook; isCopied already reflects the copied window and resets itself.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.selectableItems
params.description: The options in the same order as they render: `SelectorOptionData`, or any option type with a string `value` and an optional `disabled`. Options with `disabled` cannot be picked and are skipped while moving through the open list; ArrowDown or ArrowUp that opens the list from `onKeyDown` still lands on the first or last option.

params.name: options.isOpen
params.description: Whether the list is shown. The caller owns this state.

params.name: options.onOpen
params.description: Called to show the list. Return `false` to refuse; the hook then leaves the highlight alone.

params.name: options.onClose
params.description: Called when the hook hides the list; the hook resets the highlight first. When the caller closes the list itself (an outside press, say), it should also call `setHighlightedIndex(-1)`.

params.name: options.listboxId
params.description: The listbox element's id. Option ids are derived from it through `getItemId`.

params.name: options.value
params.description: The selected value. Without search, opening by a press, Enter or Space highlights it, or the first option when nothing is selected; ArrowDown and ArrowUp open on the first and last option.

params.name: options.onSelect
params.description: Called with the picked value. Picking also closes the list.

params.name: options.onClear
params.description: Clears the value. When provided, Delete or Backspace on the closed control clears it, so clearing is not pointer-only. Ignored while the list is open or with `hasSearch`.

params.name: options.hasSearch
params.description: Whether the list has its own search field. Space then types instead of picking, opening by a press or Enter does not pre-highlight (ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the first and last option), and printable keys on the closed control go to `onSearchSeed`.

params.name: options.onSearchSeed
params.description: With `hasSearch`, receives each printable character except Space typed while the control has focus, opening the list first when it is closed, so type-to-find needs no separate open step.

params.name: options.isDisabled
params.description: Whether the control ignores clicks and keys.

returns.name: highlightedIndex
returns.description: Index of the active option, or -1 when none is active. With `hasSearch`, opening by a press or Enter does not set one, so it stays -1 after the hook itself closes the list; ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the first or last option. Render it as the active option and name it in `aria-activedescendant` only while it points at a rendered option.

returns.name: setHighlightedIndex
returns.description: Sets the active option, for example from a filter that changes the options.

returns.name: getItemId
returns.description: The id to render on the option at `index`. Set the control's `aria-activedescendant` to `isOpen && highlightedIndex >= 0 && highlightedIndex < selectableItems.length ? getItemId(highlightedIndex) : undefined`, so it never names an option that does not exist, including in an empty list.

returns.name: onTriggerClick
returns.description: Toggles the list from a press on the control.

returns.name: onKeyDown
returns.description: Key handler for the control that keeps focus. ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list or move the active option; Enter (and Space without search) picks it or opens the list; Escape and Tab close it; Home, End, PageUp and PageDown jump to the first or last option. An editable control that keeps Home and End for the caret does not pass them to this handler, as CommandPalette does.

returns.name: onItemSelect
returns.description: Picks an option from a press on it, then closes the list.

returns.name: onItemMouseEnter
returns.description: Makes the hovered option active without scrolling the list or moving focus.

returns.name: getFieldProps
returns.description: Props for a single-line `input` you render: `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls` only while the listbox renders (`isOpen` with at least one option), `aria-activedescendant` only while an option is active, and the field’s key handler. Pass your own `onKeyDown` here rather than beside the spread: it runs after the hook’s handler unless that handler claimed the key, and it may be typed for its element.

returns.name: getListboxProps
returns.description: Props for the listbox you render, anywhere in the document, including the page’s flow: its `id` and `role`, and a press handler that keeps focus in the field. Render it while `isOpen` and there are options, and name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

returns.name: getOptionProps
returns.description: Props for the option at `index`: its `id`, `role`, `aria-selected` (true on the active option), `aria-disabled` on a disabled one, a pointer move that makes it active without moving focus, and a press that picks it.

usage.description: Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an “add people” field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.

bestPractices.description: Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and set the control's `aria-activedescendant` only while `isOpen` and `highlightedIndex` points at a rendered option, as CommandPalette does.
For type-to-select without a search field, run useTypeahead's handler first and fall through to this `onKeyDown` when it returns false, as Selector does.
For a field you render, spread the prop getters, and set the active option yourself when a new query changes the options: the first option so Enter picks it, or -1 so Enter stays the field’s.
Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query (AST-075 DEC-2). When nothing matches, announce the words the field shows for it.
Render controls that are not options, such as a create button or an empty message, inside the listbox; render them beside it.
Move DOM focus onto the options; the active option is announced through `aria-activedescendant` while focus stays on the control.

accessibility.name: Focus stays in the field
accessibility.description: With the prop getters, moving the active option never moves focus out of the field. The field names the active option through `aria-activedescendant` and carries none while no option is active.

accessibility.name: Expanded state follows the list
accessibility.description: While the listbox renders, the field exposes `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` naming it. Otherwise it exposes `aria-expanded="false"` and references nothing.

accessibility.name: Roles
accessibility.description: The field is a `combobox` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`. The list is a `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected="true"` on the active one. You name the field and the listbox.

accessibility.name: Keys
accessibility.description: While the list shows, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the active option and wrap; Enter picks an active option and only then stops the field’s own Enter; Escape, whatever modifier is held, hides the list without closing an enclosing dialog or popover on the same press. While it is hidden, ArrowDown shows it when there are options. An open field with no options still takes Escape, which closes the list, so render an empty message while it is open. Home, End, other chords such as Shift+Enter, and every other key reach the field.

accessibility.name: Input method
accessibility.description: No key moves, picks or hides while an input method is composing text.

accessibility.name: Pointer
accessibility.description: Moving the pointer over an option makes it active without moving focus; pressing an option picks it, and the field keeps focus through the press.

accessibility.name: Result count
accessibility.description: Yours to announce: compose useAnnounce (AST-075 DEC-2) so each new query announces the number of options, or that there are none, once and politely. For none, announce the words the field shows.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object for the reveal container. Optional.

params.name: options.isEnabled
params.description: When false the hook is inert: the container gets no styles and content getters return no styles, so content is always shown. Read on every render, so a component can flip it after mount (e.g. revealOn === "hover").

returns.name: getContainerProps
returns.description: Spread onto the container whose hover/focus-within drives the reveal. Accepts hoverDelay (ms the pointer must dwell before the reveal starts: a hover-intent gate like Tooltip's and HoverCard's delay, so a cursor sweeping across a list leaves nothing painted behind it) and forceState ("active" | "inactive") to pin the trigger state when a caller owns it: a motion gate, a scroll, or a row whose menu is open. "inactive" still yields to keyboard focus and coarse pointers.

returns.name: getContentRevealProps
returns.description: Spread onto each revealed / concealed child. Accepts isRevealInverted to conceal-on-hover instead of reveal-on-hover, isLayoutPreserved to reserve the layout box while hidden (opacity-only) and avoid layout shift, and forceVisibility ("shown" | "hidden") to pin this one element's appearance whatever the container is doing. "hidden" yields to focus.

usage.description: A headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it when the container is hovered or receives keyboard focus: the classic "row actions appear on hover" pattern. The reveal is CSS-only: no hover state lives in React and hovering never triggers a re-render. The caller authors no StyleX for the reveal itself; the hook hands out the container and content styles, and a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus into one another. Accessible by construction: revealed content is visually hidden at rest with position and opacity (never display:none), so it stays mounted, keeps its place in the tab order, and is announced to assistive technology; it reveals on :focus-within so keyboard users see it when tabbing in, stays visible on touch (never gated behind hover on coarse pointers), and honors prefers-reduced-motion.

bestPractices.description: Destructure getContainerProps and getContentRevealProps; spread getContainerProps() on the container (via mergeProps with your own stylex.props) and getContentRevealProps() on the content to reveal.
Use for secondary affordances: reveal-on-hover row actions (edit/copy/remove on list or table rows) and overlay controls on a card or media tile (e.g. Thumbnail's remove button).
Gate the reveal with isEnabled when a consumer prop decides whether content is revealed on hover or always shown; it can change at any time.
Pass isLayoutPreserved for absolutely-positioned or overlay content to reserve its box and avoid layout shift when it appears.
Set a hoverDelay (100-250ms) on rows in a long list, so a cursor travelling across the list does not light up every row it passes; keyboard and touch still reveal immediately.

Reach for forceState when something other than the pointer owns the interaction (a drag, a scroll or motion gate, an open row menu), and forceVisibility when just one element should ignore the container.
Reach past the API into the hook's private custom properties (--_reveal-opacity and friends) to suppress a reveal; use forceState / forceVisibility, which survive a rename.
Use it to hide content that must always be discoverable; keep essential actions visible instead of gating them behind hover.

usage.description: Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if a Tab from inside it moves focus out. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. A Tab pressed while focus is outside the container is left to the page, so an open non-modal surface never takes over the focus order of the page. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.

bestPractices.description: Call focusFirst() when opening a dialog/modal to move focus into the trapped region.
Provide an onEscape callback to close the dialog when Escape is pressed.
Rely on the built-in focus restoration on close; only add your own onHide focus handling when you need to send focus somewhere other than the previously-focused element.
Use on non-modal content like tooltips or dropdowns; those need light-dismiss, not focus trapping.

returns.name: render
returns.description: Render function for the popover element. Pass placement/alignment in context mode or x/y in fixed mode. Placement/alignment are logical: they map to the self-* position-area keyword family, which resolves against the popover's own inherited direction, so RTL contexts mirror automatically in pure CSS. Pass `positioning: "custom"` in context mode to author position styles yourself via `style` (e.g. explicit anchor() insets or an anchor-size() cover): the hook keeps the popover behavior and position-anchor wiring but derives no position styles, including the automatic RTL mirroring, which becomes your responsibility. Pass `offset` (a CSS length; a number is px) in context mode for clearance from the anchor: it applies to both edges of the placement axis, so the gap survives a flip. Layers are flush by default. Context mode first renders an inert `<template>` marker in matching server and client markup. The final layer stays at that JSX position if its parent is safe; otherwise it is portaled to the nearest ancestor outside paragraphs, links, buttons, inline formatting, and structurally restricted containers. The nearest safe host keeps CSS custom properties inheriting live, while the layer preserves direction and writing mode from its JSX position. By default this resolution occurs after hydration so closed-layer DOM remains available, and it re-renders only the slot that holds the marker and the layer, not the component that called the hook (which renders again only when a resolved mount is replaced by a render call that moved to another host); `lazyMount` defers it until `show()` and unmounts the content again on hide while the marker remains. The Popover API promotes the layer to the top layer when shown, so it escapes ancestor clipping and stacking wherever it is hosted. When the layer would overflow the viewport, position-try fallbacks flip it to the opposite side; centered layers additionally slide along the alignment axis (span fallbacks) so they stay on-screen near viewport edges.

params.description: selector for focusable items in list.

params.name: options.boundarySelector
params.description: boundary selector for lists that contain nested lists (e.g. submenu flyouts); scopes items + key handling to this level.

params.name: options.wrap
params.description: whether arrow navigation wraps around at ends.

params.name: options.onEscape
params.description: callback when Escape key pressed (e.g. close menu). Also consumes the key; without it Escape passes through to the surrounding layer.

params.name: options.orientation
params.description: navigation orientation. 'horizontal' uses ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, 'vertical' uses ArrowUp/ArrowDown, 'both' accepts all four arrows.

params.name: options.hasHomeEnd
params.description: whether Home/End jump to first/last enabled item.

params.name: options.hasPaging
params.description: whether PageDown/PageUp page through a scrolling list (last/first fully visible item, then one viewport further; never wraps).

params.name: options.hasRovingTabIndex
params.description: opt into roving-tabindex ownership: hook stamps + repairs a single tab stop across items.

params.name: options.hasCaretGuard
params.description: when true, don't steal arrow keys from a nested text input/textarea mid-line or from a contenteditable.

returns.name: listRef
returns.description: ref to attach to list container element.

returns.name: handleKeyDown
returns.description: key down handler for list container.

returns.name: handleFocus
returns.description: focus handler; keeps roving tab stop in sync when hasRovingTabIndex is on (else no-op).

returns.name: focusItem
returns.description: focus specific item by index (clamped to valid range).

returns.name: focusFirst
returns.description: focus first enabled item; returns true when focused.

returns.name: focusLast
returns.description: focus last enabled item; returns true when focused.

returns.name: ownsEvent
returns.description: whether a key event is this level's vs a nested list's (boundarySelector); always true without one.

returns.name: getItems
returns.description: this level's focusable items in DOM order, scoped by boundarySelector.

usage.description: Manages keyboard navigation within linear list following WAI-ARIA menu/listbox/toolbar patterns. Supports arrow key navigation (vertical / horizontal), Home/End for boundaries, optional wrap-around, Escape to close. Suitable for dropdown menus, toolbars, any 1D focusable list.

bestPractices.description: Set orientation to 'horizontal' for toolbars + tab bars, 'vertical' for dropdown menus.
Provide onEscape callback for menus/dropdowns to return focus to trigger.
Enable hasRovingTabIndex (+ hasCaretGuard when widget can contain text inputs) for toolbar-style composites that should be a single tab stop.
Use for 2D grid navigation; prefer useGridFocus for grids + calendars.

usage.description: Detects a single-finger press-and-hold and reports where it happened, so touch users can reach affordances that a pointer gets from right-click. iOS Safari never synthesizes a contextmenu event on long-press, which makes this the only touch route into a cursor-positioned surface such as ContextMenu. The press cancels on movement, lift, multi-touch or unmount.

bestPractices.description: Use the reported point to position the surface you open, so it appears under the finger.
Pair it with the pointer contextmenu handler rather than replacing it; this hook only covers touch.
Use it for the primary action of a control; press-and-hold is undiscoverable as the only way to do something.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.menuRef
params.description: The menu or listbox root — the surface whose rows a press picks from.

params.name: options.itemSelector
params.description: Selector matching the ENABLED rows. A pointer over anything else inside the menu (a divider, a heading, a disabled row) highlights nothing.

params.name: options.triggerRef
params.description: The control that opens the menu, when a press may start there.

params.name: options.onTriggerPress
params.description: A mouse pressed the trigger, or a finger rested on it for the long-press delay: open the menu under the held pointer and return whether it opened. Return false when the press closed an open menu instead.

params.name: options.onHighlight
params.description: Move the highlight; null clears it. Defaults to moving DOM focus with preventScroll onto the row, and onto the menu root when there is no row; after a pointer press that focus does not match :focus-visible. A picker that highlights through aria-activedescendant supplies its own.

params.name: options.onActivate
params.description: Act on the row under the release. Defaults to dispatching a click on the row that carries the release button and modifier keys.

params.name: options.onDismiss
params.description: A MOUSE was released outside the menu with nothing acting: close it. A finger released outside leaves the menu open, so this is never called then.

params.name: options.getScroller
params.description: The element to scroll while a tracked pointer rests near its top or bottom edge. Defaults to the menu root when it overflows.

params.name: options.longPressDelayMs
params.description: How long a finger must rest on the trigger before the menu opens under it.

params.name: options.isEnabled
params.description: Whether the model is live.

returns.name: menuProps
returns.description: Spread onto the menu root. Claims presses that begin inside it and marks the root as carrying the press model.

returns.name: triggerProps
returns.description: Spread onto the trigger: a mouse press opens the menu at once; a finger held for the delay opens it with the finger still down.

returns.name: isTriggerClickFromPress
returns.description: Whether the click reaching the trigger belongs to the gesture that just pressed it. That press already opened or closed the menu, so the click must neither toggle nor reopen.

returns.name: cancel
returns.description: End the gesture in flight with nothing acting, for when the menu closes under it.

usage.description: The press model of macOS and iOS menus, for any pointer: the row under the pointer when it is RELEASED is the row that acts, the highlight follows the pointer while it is held, a mouse opens the menu on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger held on the trigger opens it with the finger still down. The pointer is tracked at document level by pointerId, so a finger that slid off the row it landed on is still followed; the click the browser reports at the end of a touch, aimed at the row where the touch began, is swallowed so nothing acts twice. DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, DropdownMenuSubMenu, Selector and the menu bottom sheet already mount it; reach for it directly only when building a menu-like surface of your own.

bestPractices.description: Pass a selector for ENABLED rows only, so a disabled row or a divider under the pointer clears the highlight instead of lighting up.
Let the default highlight move focus in a menu; supply onHighlight only for a listbox that must keep focus on its combobox and highlight through aria-activedescendant.

Declare touch-action on the menu root: pinch-zoom when its rows fit, pan-y pinch-zoom when it scrolls, so the browser — not the hook — decides when a finger is scrolling, and a two-finger pinch still zooms the page.
Act on a row from its own pointerdown or pointerup handler as well; the hook already activates the row under the release, and a second path acts twice.
Read a row click with detail 0 as a keyboard activation; the hook dispatches its pointer activation with detail 0 too. Use isMenuPressActivation() to tell them apart.

params.description: config.

params.name: options.menuRef
params.description: menu / listbox root.

params.name: options.itemSelector
params.description: selector for ENABLED rows; anything else clears.

params.name: options.triggerRef
params.description: the control that opens the menu.

params.name: options.onTriggerPress
params.description: mouse press / held finger on trigger: open, return whether it opened (false = the press closed it).

params.name: options.onHighlight
params.description: move highlight (null clears); default = focus w/ preventScroll (not :focus-visible after a pointer press), menu root when no row.

params.name: options.onActivate
params.description: act on row under release; default = dispatch click w/ release button + modifiers.

params.name: options.onDismiss
params.description: MOUSE released outside: close. Finger: never called.

params.name: options.getScroller
params.description: element to edge-autoscroll while tracking; default = menu root if it overflows.

params.name: options.longPressDelayMs
params.description: finger hold before open, ms.

params.name: options.isEnabled
params.description: false = inert.

returns.name: menuProps
returns.description: spread on menu root (claims presses, marks the root).

returns.name: triggerProps
returns.description: spread on trigger (press-open, held-finger open).

returns.name: isTriggerClickFromPress
returns.description: true = the trigger click belongs to the press that already opened / closed; ignore it.

returns.name: cancel
returns.description: end the gesture w/o acting.

usage.description: Release decides; highlight follows the pointer; mouse press-opens; held finger opens. Use directly only for a menu-like surface of your own.

bestPractices.description: itemSelector = ENABLED rows only.
Default focus highlight in menus; onHighlight only for aria-activedescendant listboxes.
touch-action on the root: pinch-zoom when rows fit, pan-y pinch-zoom when it scrolls.
Also act on pointerdown / pointerup in the row; the hook already acts on release.
Treat a detail-0 row click as keyboard; the hook dispatches w/ detail 0 too — use isMenuPressActivation().

params.name: refs
params.description: Up to six refs that should all receive the same element.

returns.name: ref
returns.description: A merged callback ref that remains stable until an input ref changes.

usage.description: Combines multiple object or callback refs into one stable callback ref. Use it when a component must forward a consumer ref while also attaching internal refs. Unlike calling mergeRefs during render, the callback identity stays stable across unrelated rerenders, so React does not detach and reattach the element.

bestPractices.description: Use useMergedRefs when one element must receive both a forwarded ref and one or more internal refs.
Call mergeRefs directly in a JSX ref prop; that creates a new callback on every render and forces unnecessary detach and attach work.

params.name: refs
params.description: refs that should all receive the same element.

returns.name: ref
returns.description: stable merged callback ref; changes only when an input ref changes.

usage.description: Use when one element needs a forwarded consumer ref plus internal refs. Keeps the callback stable across unrelated rerenders.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.selectableItems
params.description: The options in the same order as they render. Options with `disabled` cannot be toggled and are skipped while moving through the open list; ArrowDown or ArrowUp that opens the list still lands on the first or last option.

params.name: options.isOpen
params.description: Whether the list is shown. The caller owns this state.

params.name: options.onOpen
params.description: Called to show the list. Return `false` to refuse; the hook then leaves the highlight alone.

params.name: options.onClose
params.description: Called to hide the list. The highlight resets first.

params.name: options.onToggle
params.description: Called with the value of the option to add or remove. Toggling keeps the list open.

params.name: options.listboxId
params.description: The listbox (or grid) element's id. Option and action-cell ids are derived from it.

params.name: options.hasSearch
params.description: Whether the list has its own search field. Space then types instead of toggling, opening by a press or Enter does not pre-highlight (ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the first and last option), Delete and Backspace edit the query, and type-to-select is off. Home and End still jump to the first and last option, so a search input that keeps them for the caret should stop them before this handler and rely on PageUp and PageDown.

params.name: options.onClear
params.description: Clears every selected value. When provided, Delete or Backspace on the closed control clears them, so clearing is not pointer-only. Ignored while the list is open or with `hasSearch`.

params.name: options.hasValue
params.description: Whether anything is selected. The Delete and Backspace clear is skipped when false.

params.name: options.isGrid
params.description: Whether each row pairs an option cell with an action cell. The inline-end arrow then moves the highlight to the row's action and the inline-start arrow back, following visual direction in right-to-left layouts, and Enter on the action runs `onActivateAction` instead of toggling.

params.name: options.rowHasAction
params.description: In a grid, whether the row at `index` has an action cell to move to.

params.name: options.onActivateAction
params.description: In a grid, runs the control in the highlighted row's action cell. The selection does not change.

params.name: options.isDisabled
params.description: Whether the control ignores clicks and keys.

returns.name: highlightedIndex
returns.description: Index of the active row, or -1 when none is active.

returns.name: setHighlightedIndex
returns.description: Sets the active row, for example after filtering. The highlight lands on the row's option cell.

returns.name: highlightedCell
returns.description: Which cell of the active row is highlighted; `'action'` only in a grid.

returns.name: activeDescendantId
returns.description: The id to pass as the control's `aria-activedescendant`: the active option, or its action cell in a grid. Undefined while the list is closed or nothing is active.

returns.name: getItemId
returns.description: The id to render on the option at `index`.

returns.name: getActionCellId
returns.description: In a grid, the id to render on the action cell of row `index`.

returns.name: onTriggerClick
returns.description: Toggles the list from a press on the control.

returns.name: onKeyDown
returns.description: Key handler for the control that keeps focus. ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list or move the active row; Enter (and Space without search) toggles the active option and keeps the list open; Escape and Tab close it; Home, End, PageUp and PageDown jump to the first or last option; without search, typed characters move to the first option whose label starts with them.

returns.name: onItemMouseEnter
returns.description: Makes the hovered option, or its action cell, active without scrolling the list or moving focus.

usage.description: Tracks the active option of a multi-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers MultiSelector; unlike useCombobox, toggling an option keeps the list open, and rows can carry an action cell. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control and the list, and wires the ARIA attributes from what it returns.

bestPractices.description: Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and pass `activeDescendantId` as the control's `aria-activedescendant`.
Use `isGrid` only when rows carry a control next to the option; give each action cell `id={getActionCellId(index)}`.
Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query.
Close the list after each toggle; a multi-select stays open so several options can be picked in a row.

Expect an item for a nested heading, such as one in a blockquote. Only root headings become items.
